I don't know why, but about 3 months ago, my cat suddenly got it in his head that he wanted to be fed between 5 and 6am. He's seven years old, and he's never been fed that early! His normal feeding time had always been somewhere between 8 and 9am, so this was something completely new, different and unwelcome. Well, after a few weeks of the cat's incessant whining starting around 5am, he finally trained me to get up, throw some dry food in his bowl, then stumble back to bed. Once he gets something to eat, not only does he quiet down, but he jumps up on the bed and goes back to sleep himself. I discovered that if he gets something to eat between 5 and 6am, the  cat alarm  no longer goes off even at 8 (his old usual time), and I get to sleep later than ever. But I really didn't enjoy dragging myself up out of bed in the early hours of the morning just to give the cat a small handful of dry food.Enter the Cat Mate C10 Automatic Pet Feeder!I'm going to cut to the chase here. Before I bought it, I read all the reviews. Of the more negative things that people report, I have seen no sign. The cat doesn't bat the feeder around trying to get to the food, nor indeed, does he spend any time trying to figure out how to open it. The battery doesn't keep falling out (though I will say, I don't understand why they don't have a little plastic cover for the battery compartment). The timer is accurate enough, for my cat, anyway.This simple and inexpensive unit has been a life-saver...or at least, a sleep-saver.

My work schedule changed so I needed a feeder with timer that didn't show the food that was going to be dispensed.Thought this would work.Have tried it 4 times, each time he gets it open and eats his food way before his meal time.So since it wasn't inexpensive am returning it.Might work for others, it just didn't for my pet.

UpdateI really liked this feeder as I stated below but 4 months after  both sides are not working anymore. The lids are off and my cat was not even trying to open them. I have tried to put tape but obviously it does not work. Very disappointed given the price, it is not a good deal.I was really looking for an automatic feeder for my cat. This works perfect! I work from 9-6 and my cat eats mostly wet food, so to keep her to be extra hungry and give me an one hour of loud complains when I get home, I tried this one. I followed others suggestions and put a transparent tape underneath to keep the battery in place ( I agree with many reviews that the design is faulty), but once done, everything works well ( for me at least).The lids open every time at the specific time. I have a great cloud camera so I can see at what time it does open from work. And i have an active inquisitive young cat and she hasn't been able to open before time ( perhaps 10min before only when the lid is starting to be loose). I saw this also with the camera.The can - I put one 2.8 can stays fresh and she always eats all.My only complain is that I use only one side for one feeding so I always need to remember to turn it off so the lids do not open in the middle of the night. You need to set them up to be able to close them.they open at 0.I recommend it to working cat  parents  with long hours and a wet-only cat feeding among others if course!

I spent a lot of time researching food dispensers before buying several of these. If you are serving dry kibble, you have a few more options, but for serving canned and/or raw food this is the best choice I've found so far. I tried a rotating feeder and the design was really wacky - the lid rotated while the base stood still, which was completely awkward. Plus it broke before I even got to test it on my cats.I used these feeders a few times when going away for a night or two, and using two of these with one cat worked pretty well (so the cat was able to get four meals) since the timer goes up to 48 hours. The only real problem then is that the ice pack is awful. It's small and thin and doesn't stay cold for that long. It helps to freeze the food in the trays ahead of time as well, but there is enough room in the base of the feeder that it COULD take a much larger ice pack (or two of the smaller ones) with just a slight redesign, but they've made a preformed plastic  wall  where the little ice pack goes, so it's very limited in there.My next problem came when I wanted to use these feeders with more than one cat. Each cat eats in a separate feeding  cube  that they reach through an automated door, but the timer on this thing is rather imprecise, and the cats are not going to get their food at the same time. Even though they are eating in different areas, it's not like they don't know that another cat  got fed  and they haven't yet. Since they don't understand why, I don't really want to do that to them.Finally, and the reason I will never use these feeders again...I came home one time and one of the feeding stations for one of my cats hadn't deployed. That is pretty much my worst nightmare of leaving my cats alone for a day or two - that the feeder won't work and they won't get their food. Even worse that two of them did and the third one just had to go hungry while watching the others eat. The timer has to twist around until it gets to a little notch and then the door is supposed to spring up - it's pretty low-tech which I kind of think is a good thing, but I really need 100% reliability in a product like this. I would pay a lot more money to have something that can connect to my network and send me an email to tell me everything is a-ok...or maybe just a pet sitter?

I highly suggest this for any cat owners that have demanding breakfast eaters,

My German Shepherd loved it for the 20 or so minutes that it was in one piece. Ferrets are carnivorous, that's right they eat meat. Not berries, not bananas, not rice, not corn, not wheat, not sugar. The only time they would eat vegetation is when they consume and animal such as a rabbit and they eat it's stomach contents. Does this mean ferrets are the small animal kingdom equivalent to pit bulls and will attack your family members? No! Do they bite? Nip? Yes like any other animal you would bring into your house. Keeping your ferret on this food and this food alone with shorten their life spans, and health problems will happen more easily. I have three ferrets, a Boy who is 5 years old and two girls who are 1. My boy will live till at least 12 or 13. Always keep an eye out for blood (sometimes these bones can be chewed into sharp edges that can cut your dog's gums- not usually a huge issue, but keep an eye out for it). Also, make sure your dog isn't managing to chew off large pieces and swallowing them, and once the bone gets to a size you think your dog might want to swallow, remove it and replace with a new one. I have heard of dogs cracking teeth on nylabones, but if your dog's teeth are in good shape that shouldn't be a huge concern (I keep my dog's teeth in great shape with a combination of high quality diet, daily dental chews- greenies are my dog's favorite, nylabones, and monthly tooth brushing. I could kick all those stories that say  give kitty a saucer of milk .  WRONG!  Don't take chances with your kittiy's life.I have fostered dozens of motherless kittens over the years, many of which were malnourished, and have had wonderful success bottle feeding kittens with KMR.  It is packed with nutrition - protein, vitamins and calories for growing infant kittens.  They do VERY well with KMR.  It is also great to mix with wet kitten food to wean kittens from bottle feeding.  Long story, but I had a kitten who needed to be on a liquid diet for life.  I fed her this formula mixed with special wet food and water to make it liquid.  She did very well on this formula for many years.  Be sure to only mix as much as you are going to use right away, and keep unused portions in the freezer for best nutrition and longest shelf life.  It doesn't keep for a long period of time.  Read the instructions on the bag/package.  KMR is offered in a variety of sizes.  PS This is also an excellent supplement for a sick or underweight cat to get extra nutrition into the cat, or to give extra nutrition to a nursing mom cat (who should be spayed as soon as the kittens stop nursing).  Most cats love it, just mix according to package instructions and offer it in a small shallow bowl or saucer.  Shallow so as not to have their whiskers hit the sides of the bowl.  Cats hate that!  :)

One note; I was told this size crate is good for a BELGIAN MALINOIS that is fully grown -- it is TOO SMALL! I'm actually going to sell it on Crags List so that I can get the XXL crate from Midwest Life Stages -- they DO MAKE AN OUTSTANDING PRODUCT!
This is a standard kennel - what you would expect.  It's perfect for my 3 lb Boston Terrier, because as she goes, I will move the divider.

The assembly was a little tricky.  Its packed fastened together for shipping and I had a time trying to figure it out, even mashed my finger a time or two.  Once its together, though, its a great crate for my dog.  Dual latches and there don't seem to be any jagged edges for him to hurt himself.

I purchased this for a new puppy. To begin with, this was a breeze to setup. I've had to deal with some clunky crates in the past that require a degree in engineering to set up. This didn't even require the instructions. I can tear it down and have it back up within a few minutes. Quite honestly, it takes me longer to take the dog's toys out of the crate.It came with the divider to section it off, which was helpful. The thing I liked most though -- the two doors. The spot I have the crate is against two walls. Most crates have only the one door and this wouldn't have worked for my purposes. I love having the option.  All in all, a well-made product.
I like this crate.  I bought it for a puppy so really liked that you can divide it as the dog grows

We bought this crate, and a soft-sided kennel for a husky puppy.  We are not using the soft-sided crate at all, because it's so huge the puppy will use it for the bathroom.  However, this kennel lets us set up a divider while the puppy grows, which we're finding is a MUST.  We read articles saying this, but I liked the look of the soft-sided crates, so got both.  Should have just went for this kennel and then considered a soft-sided crate for when the dog is much bigger and already potty trained.  You do not need both for the beginning (unless you want a crate to keep in the car).  The kennel IS heavy, so I can't imagine moving it around the house from one location to another at different times. Super easy to put together.
This crate collapses very easily and can be lifted up with a convenient handle. We really like the crate, just wish it was a bit taller so our dog (pit bull) could sit upright without hunching.
Great for our 55 lb German Shepherd.  Quality on these are awesome.

This is a super easy crate to assemble and fold up (if necessary).  My Dobie is about 75 lbs. and this crate is just barely big enough.  I wish I would have gone one size bigger, but it's close enough.  The dual access doors are handy.  I saw this same style crate on Caesar 911 after I bought it and thought,  Man, if Caesar uses it...  it must be a good crate.   Very happy with the crate!

Easy to assemble, well-made, & sturdy - however with one swipe of the paw, our dog can open the door.  We don't use the crate for when we're away, so this isn't a big deal for us, but if you're looking for a sturdy crate with a door that will stay locked, know that these doors latch in a very loose, almost flimsy way.  In other crates, you have to lift the handle, then close it, then push the handle down...however for this one, you can just slide it back and forth.  If your dog makes any effort at all to leave, believe me, they will!

This is a very well made crate - I have two little cairn terriers who are very exuberant and I often need to crate them while I do things around the house because the get under foot a lot.  I love the fact that it has two doors - one on the side and one on the front.  Makes it more versatile.  I bought one of these years ago which I have in my great room, and recently bought another to put in the bedroom.  The dogs like to go in there and take a nap of their own volition.  Its their own little space...  :)

Since I've never used any other dog crate I can't compare to anything else, all I know is that this thing was easy to assemble and has held together superbly. The latches seem to be very durable as well and our puppy has never gotten out, even when he was little and pounded on the doors when he was getting used to it (sad Mama--but for the record, now he loves it and doesn't spend alot of time locked up in it). I also lvoe that it has a second door so we can move it anywhere in the house without worrying about access.It was really nice that it came with an extra  life stages  panel so that when he was a puppy we could block off most of the cage. The panel can be installed in any part of the cage since it just hooks on to the exterior bars. Although the panel was a bit tricky to move each time, so we just did it twice and then opened up the whole cage when we knew our puppy wouldn't soil inside the crate.I never noticed any extra noise with the pan. We always had a blanket and now there's a memory foam bed inside.
This crate is well constructed and the water bowl we got to attach on the inside is her favorite watering hole.

My entire family uses these crates.  I have one that is over 7 years old.  It has survived two of our boxers and now a puppy.  My 6 year old 65 pound boxer loves it so much that he rather sleep in it than the couch.  I do need to get a new plastic bottom for it since it has several holes but what do you expect after 7 years.  I just bought another to keep my puppy in at night since she was causing too much trouble.  The price can also not be beat.I don't understand people saying it has rough spots.  I check every spot on my new one and don't see even one spot my puppy can hurt herself on or that I can hurt myself on.  It is also very sturdy.  I will admit that it isn't escape proof if your dog really tries for hours to escape but if you do proper crate training, your dog won't want to escape.

Size is just right for my dog, construction is great, easy to set up, two doors. What more can you ask for?Updated 5/23/14:Somehow, my crafty dog managed to get out of this crate the other day while I was at work. I keep carabiner clips on the door latches so he can't get out that way, but one whole end of the crate had detached from the sides with the carabiner still keeping the door latched! I don't think his ability to escape is a fault with the crate; more than likely some hook had come undone and I didn't notice it.  So just be sure you check them occasionally to make sure they're all secure. As an extra protection, I have now put cable ties where each end meets the sides and so far 'Houdini' hasn't cracked it. Since I don't need the crate to be mobile, this solution is fine, and if I need to disassemble the crate for moving, I can just cut them off.
Great crate!  Easy to put together & love the 'double latch' on the door!  Thanks for a great product!
Great crate.  Easy to set up and take down and very secure.  I have yet to have my dog escape.  It's not near as heavy as my older wire crate is and its much easier to take places and set up.

My crate came dented and slightly out of shape.  Because it is fairly sturdy, it took a little muscle to bend the front part with the one door back to where I could secure both latches.  Midwest products are great.  This is my second double door folding crate I have of Midwest.

I wanted something that would easily collapse when not in use and this fits the bill. It is a little heavy perhaps for some (I think somewhere around 15-20lbs) but I don't mind the weight. Perfect size and hope it will last for years to come! It even has a divider to make it easy to crate train a puppy which is a nice feature, although not much use now as my dog is past her puppy stage. Would be nice if they made that feature an option instead of coming with as now I have this metal piece I will never use and just extra parts laying around. Overall would recommend this as a good, sturdy crate.
Good crate, has started to get a little flimsy. Also is hell to clean if your dog gets poop in between the wire.

This is my second crate. The first was for the new untrained (large) puppy. This worked wonders for potty-training, and she likes having 'her own' space the other dog is not allowed in. My older, already trained dog seemed so interested in the crate for the puppy that I bought this second one. Now each dog has it's own place. With an added pillow, the dogs will stay in their crates while I'm busy. The dogs also choose to sleep in them. I seldom close the doors on them, but neither dog minds much if I close them in because they can still see everything. I especially appreciate these because they fold down easily for transportation. When we go on vacation the dogs can come along now, too.

I just got the crate and found that the divider was dented on one side.No biggie though.It was a bit tough to get all hooked up but at least that means it wouldn't be easy for it to come apart if the pup is rambunctious (mine isn't) but most puppies including mine like to play so it is reassuring to know that it won't fall apart on him.One thing that is a bit annoying is that there are clips that kept everything together when folded.  When it is all set up though there is no place for the clips to hide or clip onto and sticks out on the side like a sore thumb.Another thing that kind of bothers me is that the latch for the doors isn't curved at the end like many I have had and seen.  It is just straight so I'm not sure it that will keep it locked if the puppy were to get really bouncy in there.If the latch is all the way down, the  handle  part of it is attached on the underside of the straight part so it gets caught on the crate door  preventing  it from just moving.

We had bought our lab mix a crate like this but a few sixes smaller. We had thought it would be the perfect size for him when he was full grown, but he's grown like a weed. Our first crate only had one door which was fine, but the second door has proven to be very helpful in just the month that we've had it. We put it in our bedroom for him to sleep in and its nice to have the longer side against the wall so we aren't tripping over it. We haven't put it in our car for a trip yet, but if he's going to be riding in it, the second door will make it easier to get him in and out. It also does fold up pretty easily so if you are packing to take it somewhere it doesn't take up the whole car.

I love midwest crates due to quality, price and versatility.  This crate has a black coating on the metal, 2 seperate doors for entering when at a show and space is at a premium, folds down into a suitcase for portability and has a tray on the bottom to collect spills.

Really a nice crate, and well priced.  Unfortunately, the END door latches on the crate we received were not welded in proper alignment with the crate walls, so it has to be forced closed.  Such a simple thing, and at first not too important because of the way we used it.  Now, wanting to use the end door rather than the side door, this dysfunction has become annoying, especially in the dark in the middle of the night!

This crate was absolutely perfect for my English Springer Spaniel.  When she was a new puppy, we put the divider in halfway and had a small dog bed in there for her.  As she grew, we extended it and turned her bed sideways.  Now that she's 5 months old and 35 pound - we've removed the divider and bought her a full sized dog bed.  She's got room to finish growing and she's never had ONE accident in there.  What I found amazingly cute - and a way to keep this in a central part of the house and not all cold and steely - was a crate cover that I got on Etsy.  Because this create is such a standard and common size, I was able to find a  custom  crate cover in the cutest fabrics that matches my decor *and* provides my dog her cave like privacy.  I highly recommend this crate as a dog owner's staple and then a crate cover as a way to make it a true part of any home.

Love this crate! the two doors make it easy to put in any corner and it looks great to! It's well made and my dog loves it! The price and durability is worth picking this crate. I have had dogs all my life and this is one of the better crates I've invested in. Thank you!
A metal crate with double-doors is perfect if you are placing a dog into the hatch area of an SUV as it allows for easier enterering/leaving the crate.

We bought this crate for our puppy just about 2 years ago.  It worked perfectly.  We have been on several long road trips with the dog and required we take the crate.  It folded up and set up easily.  We still have it set up at the house and the dog uses it as place to sleep at times.  I recommend this product.
Prefect crate, two doors which is nice especially when in the car, you don't have to situate it a certain way because there is only a front door so that is nice for travelling and just everyday use.

I like the way this crate has two openings and a tray that comes right out for cleaning. The only thing I'd change is maybe to have one latch to open from the top instead of two. My little dog almost can't wait for the second one to be opened before she tries to come dashing out!

We purchased this for our lab/terrier mix. At 4 months he's already 35 lbs and fits well within this crate. The only reason I'm giving it 4 stars is because during the first time assembling the crate there were a couple pieces that were joined with the pieces below. I couldn't detach, worked on it for over 20 minutes. Finally after much pulling and pushing I was able to detach from the piece below. Now that we've used for over a month and taken with us camping, I've never had the same problem.The other thing I'm a little disappointed is I can't find a good weather resistant crate cover for this size. I've looked all over online and most I've found are for a different brand and the measurements don't fit or they are crate covers for this size but for decorative appeal, not for traveling.Overall, I'm very impressed with the quality, size and price.

I've had these types of crates before and they are a life saver for crating your dog while house training them and for when they are left alone. Also for sleeping in. The divider that comes with it is SUPER helpful in lowering the possibility that he/she will potty where he sleeps. The only problems I have with these crates is that they can be a little difficult putting together/folding up. It's not as simple as you'd think. Also, installing and uninstalling the divider takes two people if you're not super strong. But there are not many other styles of crates out there that have the same qualities as this one.
It will be the adult kennel one day. The only thing I do not like is that the side gate and movable barrier do not allow me to place two smaller pups one on each side.
Tough and well made. This is one of the best crates..Only negative is Midwest and many others have gone to plastic trays. The tray doesnt last...MIDWEST, Sale the metal trays!..Please!

We got this for our (now) 50 Lbs. Australian Shepherd.  It's easy to latch and unlatch and he seems perfectly comfortable in there though we very rarely put him in there anymore.  It folds down easily enough for toting.  Good product

Got this crate for training my Sheltie.  I also purchased the casters for the bottom, which makes this crate easy to move around as during the day I would keep it in my kitchen and at night I would roll it into my bedroom.  I have had this product for over a year now and have successfully used it to house train and keep my Sheltie safe while I am not at home.  My dog is fully housebroken now and I 'm only required to use it when I'm not at home, but she is so used to it that she frequently goes in it on her own when the mood strikes her.  It is easily portable and I will place it in my car when I want to take my dog with me.  Occasionally, she gets car sick and when she does, I can easily remove the platform and wash it out.  If I have the crate in my car and I need to use the third row seats, it folds up easily and fits behind the third row seats.  It's the only way to have a dog.

The divider is not wide enough for a medium size pup, and I was buying this to use like a pet apartment.Instead of cutting a hole in the divider like the pet apartment has in it, I put the divider in at an angle and used velcro strips to secure the divider in place.I used cloth and velcro to cover the opposite end so the hooks would not be an issue.Love it!  Puppy sleeps well, potties as needed opposite side, and we are one happy puppy family!
this is a little smaller than we expected.  good quality and okay size for a young kitten which is what we bought it for--easy for small kitten to climb into!

The humane society I volunteer at uses this pooper scooper for their exercise yards and it works so great, I bought one for myself. They have had this pooper scooper for over a year, they use it at least twice a day, and it's still in good condition. I like how you don't have to bend over at all and how one side is a rake and the other solid. If you open them all the way, you can use a single side to either rake poo into a more easy-to-scoop pile, or you can use the solid side to slide quickly under poo on concrete. The scoops are also very easy to clean, especially if you spray them with bleach spray and let it soak for a few minutes before washing it off with warm water.We pair this with a bucket that you can find here:http://smile.amazon.com/ProSelect-Stainless-Steel-2-Quart-6-Inch/dp/B005N127KW/ref=sr_1_3?ie=UTF8&qid;=1395837954&sr;=8-3&keywords;=stainless+steel+bucketWe usually line the bucket with a plastic shopping bag. Works great and our yards are always clean for the pups.
Can't get to excited about it except it does the job and makes it easier to clean up. Have always had a pooper scooper for my dogs.

Decent product for the price.  I've just purchased my second of these scoopers.  I'd say they last about 2 years, before the rake section gets too bent to be worth much.  If you have a grassy yard, that doesn't sit level everywhere, this is the best scooper I've found.  I'd recommend, with the knowledge it'll be replaced within a couple of years.

My other one held up well for nearly 3 years but I couldn't find another one like it at the Pet Store and those plastic ones I was breaking them it seemed like every couple of months...The only reason I'm replacing this one now is because I managed to bend a couple of the rake tines...I suppose I could get some pliers and straighten it out but my girls also got a hold of it when they were about a year old and chewed up the handles pretty bad but duct tape took care of that...Seriously though this thing works great for the money...
Love the scooper. Easy to use. Perfect for grass of any length. Rinses easily. Will probably buy another one soon.

This was the largest littler pan that I could find on Amazon at the time and I was expecting it to be the same size as the standard pans I purchased at Target or Petsmart however it is several inches smaller and the wall taper makes it seem even smaller. It does the job but I probably look for a larger one next time.

These are just good sturdy standard litter boxes to have around. Not fancy, but hey, they're great if you are building a fancy enclosure. I find this was a better buy that a high sided pan I bought because they can get out and cover up waste easier.
The pan itself is great just wished the sides were taller so that when my cat flicks the litter it doesn't fly everywhere outside her kennel. It serves its purpose though. Got the blue one.
I use these pans for rearing new born rats and mice,  They are very easy to use and fit in the racks perfectly

It's a cat litter pan thingie. It sits inside of a badass piece of cat furniture so you don't even see it. I don't know how anyone can LOVE this, but hey - it's functional. It doesn't leak. It's exactly what it says it is. It didn't surprise me. What the heck else does one say about a plastic box? Esme Pyewacket (fat cat) approved.

This is my second litter pan with the rim - I actually put these in an enclosed wooden litter box, and they are the perfect size. It really helps to have the rim - of course it doesn't catch all of the litter, but one time I didn't have it on and you could most certainly see a difference! It also cleans really well.
I bought this for the local Humane society as it was what they put on their wish list.  I am guessing they like it.
Works pretty good. Picks up poop and whatnot. Kind of wish we went with the actual picker upper, but the grass is always greener, right?

I have 4 dogs and a large yard. I don't clean up everyday so when I do there is a lot there. I have to empty the pan into a larger trash bag, but I did use the advice that another person had on the reviews. I tie a grocery bag on the pan, and it not only makes it easier to empty, but it keeps the pan clean too. It is a little difficult to get the bag off without getting a little dirty, and the rake will fling pieces over the pan if you are not careful. Not a good idea to stand behind it when using the rake!
The rake set arrived in perfect condition.  It was exactly what I wanted.  It is very sturdy and well made.  Very Happy!BB

This is not built to last by any means. I ordered the large, the pan is very flimsy, a dollar store plastic dust pan has more rigidity and stability. The pan is not secured to the pole well either. How this item has nearly 5 stars with 170+ reviews is beyond me.

now the reason i gave it a 4 star is because it took a week for them to ship out. i bought it from seller (rollstone) but what i do like what they did was when they did ship it out thursday afternoon i got it friday(next day) so it was really cool and the product is awesome i am glad i went with this one and not the jaw scoop one :)
This is a great tray, especially for larger dogs. The rake is a little on the smaller side, but thats fine, no biggie. The tray is actually quite large, so perfect for our medium/large size dog.

I bought this to pick up cat waste that constantly shows up in my yard.  The set is great for that and for raking up other objects.  My only issue is that the pan is very big, making storage a problem.  I store it outside and it's a bit of an eye sore.  The other issue that I have is that the rake and the pan don't store together and the rake has to lean against something in order to stand up.  I have a large backyard and this serves its purpose, but if you live in an apartment or plan to take this with you while you walk your dog, then I wouldn't recommend it.  Otherwise, it is sturdy and built with quality materials and should last a long time.

Very sturdy and large,I wish I had ordered 2 of these when I got this one for $17 with Amazon Prime,it holds quite a bit and with having 3 large dogs it's working out great!! I have a smaller one that I paid more for at the pet store,have had it for about 4 years now and it has held up very well
Great product.  I ordered another produce previously and it was junk.  This works just fine.  Even my husband uses it.

This set beats the clam shell type design to pick up dog poop. Also doubles to pick up most anything else in the yard. I am very pleased with this set! Sturdy design and lightweight enough for me to use at age 75.
I find the rake and pan combo much easier to use than the scooper style tools that are out there. The handle is long enough to let you stay a nice distance from the job to be done.

I have three chihuahuas, one of which is an elderly dog that insists on doing his business as close to the front steps as possible. Add to that the occasional large mess from dogs just roaming the neighborhood and walking to the car in the mornings becomes a walk in a field of  landmines.  I'd tried the other type of pooper scooper...the one with the jawlike grabber...but it wasn't very efficient and ended up grabbing more grass and dirt than poo. Used this the first day out of the box and managed to gather up every little piece in my front yard in less than 5 minutes. Fantastic product and so simple. Who would have thought it?Two words of advice though:1. rake gently unless you want poo flying towards your legs b/c the rake is very elastic and will act like a catapult if used too aggressively.2. Unless you have a LOT of poo or very large specimens from large dogs, I'd go with the small (which is what I purchased). The pan is plenty large; I'd estimate it's approximately 12 x12  at the very least.
much more stable than the plastic rakes. It gets everything out of snow and grass with ease. I like that the container is big in case I don't clean up each day.

Very handy tool for doing my weekly yard clean-up.  I have a bad back and the longer handles make it so that I don't have to bend over much.  The rake works great (better than a spade in my opinion) and the large pan makes it so that I don't have to keep dumping it continuously.  A good purchase.
Guess I love it!  MAX capacity makes this easy to use and I can get several  items  retrieved in one trip.  I use a single scoop during warmer weather but this was great to have for winter clean up!
This Spade Set is made very well. I like how big it is and it it easy to clean after using it.

We just got a German Shepherd puppy and we were not sure how our daughter would prefer to pick up his leavings.  So we asked her.  We had purchased the rake type scoop for another dog in the past.  She said that left a mess and that the rake was impossible to keep clean, that it became a poo club after a few uses.  We had also gotten the kind that  grabs  the poo like an automatic shovel thing.  She said that it missed half the time.  This was just what she wanted, and she can get several piles in the scoop at once before dumping.  Very pleased.  As pleased as you can be with a utensil that picks up poo.

I wouldn't say that I am the most uncoordinated person on earth, but I sure felt like it when I was trying to scoop up after my dogs with a claw-type scooper. Actually, only of our dogs poops in inappropriate place, and she's a chihuahua, so the size of this scooper is more than sufficient, and I find it much easier to handle and operate than the claw type.
Not really that great.  I suppose the activity itself is the problem, but I don't find it particular easy with these unit and the dog loves to get a hold of them and run around.

Works like it should, durable and doesn't rust while sitting outside in the rain. When I received it in the mail I realized I used these same ones when I worked at an animal boarding kennel as a teenager, and those scooped lots and LOTS of poop from around 80 dogs multiple times a day for years!

I have had similar sets before that seemed cheaply made and didn't last long, but these are much better constructed.Although I have only had this set a few months, it seems they will likely hold up for some time with my two larger dogs.It makes poop scooping a breeze.
The scooper is made of sturdy construction and works great.  The large set allows me to do my whole yard without having to lug the trash around with me.
Best scooper! We have two dogies and they know how to do their business. Ours stay outside and has been used almost daily since we bought it and it has held up well.
This works great and it's easy to clean. Really efficient even in tall grass.
It is what it is. I find it easy to use to keep my yard clean. I am short so I find the size perfect, but someone taller might wish the handle was longer.

We've tried them all!  From the two-piece rake / scoop; to the one piece  crane  contraptions.  This is by far the best scooper we have ever used!!Ben, the 110lb cane corso that takes residence at my house, is the best at what he does.  And when he does it, well, lets say its no deer pellet!!  This scooper takes care of it in one motion!! I was amazed!!!!!  No mess, no fuss.If you have a dog, and you clean up after him, you need this scooper!

If you have grass (long or short) and you have a dog or several for that matter, this will pick up your dog's business.  I'd like if it was a little tougher / stronger metal, however it can be fixed just by pressing the metal against the ground. No big deal.  So far it has been a good utility to pick up the poop!

Honestly, I was a little skeptical since the design is so simple, but this scooper works better than any other I've had. I had a claw style scooper before, but since I only scoop once in a while, my four arm was tired after being out there for more than ten minutes and mostly it just smeared my dogs stuff in the grass rather than pick it up cleanly. This is simply a scoop that lets grass pass through, but pulls up the crap. Works great!

Yeap, I have to say I love this poop scooper.. Have used many over the years.. always a two handed job.. and I carried a bucket when we had 5 dogs and over an acre to clean.  Now have only 2 dogs and a small yard, but this is a great picker.  Takes a little getting used to, but gets even our smaller dogs poop without tearing up the lawn

Great item for large dogs. Used for the first time last week after a snow melt (that lasted the better part of 2 months). Had a lot to pick up (2 large dogs), this rake made easy work. Only suggestion would be to make the handle a little longer-took slight bending for a 6' person to use.

I've been using a plastic poop rake with a large tray for about a year now. I bought it from Petco and after 6 months two of the plastic tongues of the rake broke off.I thought this metal wire rake would do the trick. After two weeks of use I can honestly tell you what it's good for.If your dog mostly has large dry movements and you have tall grass this tool would be a lifesaver. Otherwise I think a conventional poopi rake works much better.The gap between each wire is kind of wide. So it is hard to pick up small pieces of poop. Let's say those with a diameter of under 1/2  . I realize this is much more info than you wanted to know but it's important. I have stray cats that come poop on my grass and their thin poop is difficult to pick up. Also if there is somewhat soft wet poop and you use this wire rake good luck getting it the poop off. Because of it's geometry it is hard to shake the soft wet poop off. A conventional poopi rake would work better in those situations.I can see myself buying another brand new one down the line to use as a tennis ball launcher. Pick up the ball without bending down and then heave it for my dog to chase and retrieve.  Now that sounds like fun. I just gave the seller a great marketing idea :)

I have used this for a year now.  It is great for its designed use.  I have not had any problems with bending that some others have had.  It makes an unpleasant job easier, which really is the definition of a good tool.

We use this for the grassy area where the dog goes.  It works really well at pulling just the stuff it's supposed to and not taking the grass with it.  I just wish the tines were a little closer together because some of the smaller pieces (we have a puppy) fall through occasionally.
Definitely does it's job! It is difficult when trying to pick up droppings in pine straw (pick up a ton of unwanted straw), but that will likely be the case with any scooper.
the only thing that could be improved on this is a longer handle is needed ,it's much shorter than I thought it would be
Just used it again this morning. Rakes poop up from the grass like a charm.  Older man's back likes it too.

I have two dogs that around 25-30 pounds or so, and they make plenty of messes in my back yard.  But cleanup is truly a breeze with this tool.  It's so simple.  Since you don't have the teeth that you see on some scoops. you don't get poop squished between the teeth.  (Sorry if that's TMI.  But it's an important feature for me.)  This scoop just slides right underneath the mess, and I drop it in a 2-gallon bucket that lined with a plastic grocery bag.  I've shown this scooper to a couple of friends, who also wanted it for their dogs.  And the price is definitely right.

The scoop seems well-made and is fairly easy to use. It is a little hard to dump the dog waste into a plastic bag as it tends to fall off the sides at times, but I've just started putting the bag in a bucket and that works well. For what it's worth, it works really well for picking up the blue spruce cones that fall in my yard, too--better than a rake!

The metal is strong and works well.  It doesn't flex.  I prefer this over the normal spade.  The only problems are the rake will sometime spear the poop and you have to knock it off.  Also, it doesn't help with liquidy poop but nothing really works anyways.

This pooper-scooper does just an okay job at picking up my two dogs stinky yard bombs. I sort of drifted back and forth between different scooper designs and ultimately chose the wire rake design as I thought it would be easier on my grass than the claw design which in previous experience tends to pull out grass along with dog waste.This scooper has two primary disadvantages. First, the spaces between the wires means that some of the dog waste won't be large enough to be picked up. I have two medium sized dogs (French Bulldogs) and while most of the time the wire rake design is good enough there's still a portion of waste that I have to pick up using other means. Second, the wires themselves tend to get pretty easily tangled in my grass meaning that although I'm not tearing out a lot of grass I'm still inevitably pulling some grass out. The side-effect of trying to disentangle the wires is that inevitably some of the dog waste will spill out of the basket.It's an all-metal construction with a decent rubberized grip. The length of the entire scooper is about 30-inches so you will likely end up having to bend down to scoop up the dog waste.--------------------WHAT I LIKE:(+) Good construction. This is an all metal scooper with a rubber grip; no cheap plastics here.(+) Wire rake is a bit easier on grass than claw-type scoopers--------------------WHAT COULD BE BETTER:(-) The entire scooper is about 30  but still a bit too short to prevent me from having to bend down to pick up dog waste (I'm 5'10 )(-) Some of the dog waste will inevitably fall through the wires or be too small to pick up with this scooper(-) Though easier on grass than claw-scoopers you're still very likely to rip out some grass while using this scooper--------------------CONCLUSION:This scooper gets a  just okay  rating from me. While it does a decent job the design could definitely be improved with perhaps a longer handle and more closely spaced wires.

I've gone through many scoopers in my day and I'll tell you from experience: Look no further.  This thing is perfect!  Works great, doesn't destroy the yard, and saves your back.  Just buy it if you are a dog owner, you won't regret it.

We have a 13 year old wolf hybrid and new german shepherd puppy, so I grabbed one of these based on all the good reviews (and a few that were not so good).  I had low expectations, but the price was worth a shot.  I love it.  I'm used to using a larger shovel, leaving divots in the ground and having a sore arm from all the presents left behind.  As long as the present is firm, or at least a few hours old, the rake scoops through the grass cleanly and does a tremendous job of picking it up.  Very light, very easy to use, can't believe I've gone my whole life without this.  I can see where taller people have to stoop to use this, but I do that with a shovel anyway, and a handle that is longer would make it much harder to control the rake.  Now the shovel and the hose come out only when there is an upset tummy in the house.

This dog house is a good design to keep a dog warm because it has a compact footprint, low ceiling, raised floor, and substantial walls.  The floor has some flex to it but also has stabilizers built into the bottom of the floor which keeps it from bowing too much.  This makes it difficult to put insulation underneath.  This is a problem for us because the dog chews up pads like they were breath mints. The snaps around the bottom seem to be the first thing to go.  The vent on top is a little larger than most and is recessed so it's not that easy for a dog to chew off.  I found it to be too darn small for my 80# dog.  Maybe if had shorter legs or shorter torso, but when I watched him getting in, he had to bow his back so much that I thought I'd need a doggie chiropractor, and he could barely turn around to stretch along the long side.  No way could he curl up in it.  Someone else suggested that you go up a size for an animal over 70 pounds.  I'd say that's good advice.  I didn't buy this dog house from Amazon, but thought I'd do this review while I'm here looking for a replacement.
Bought for use at animal shelterThis was on their wish list as the cats love them.They were thrilled to have it

I gave this to my friends as a  Thank You  for a bout of cat-sitting. They have a hard time finding cat toys that their dogs won't chew to shreds, so I thought this would have a fair chance of surviving.Their cats love it! The youngest (around 3) takes up the center space and tries to catch the ball as it spins, while the older cats (12 and 14) would stalk around the outside and bat at the ball as it went round and round the circle. Great for active kittens and cats! But not so good for older, less playful cats. My current cat doesn't much care for it, and only ever bat the toy inside around on occasion, but quickly loses interest.However, I have had cats in the past who just adored this toy! And it holds up very well.
The kittens love this toy. If we want to get any peace and quiet we have to hide it from them!

I got this for my two cats to help entertain them.  They batted the ball a little for a few days but quickly grew bored with this toy and no longer go near it.  One of them even threw up on it. I'm not sure if that was a statement.You get what you pay for, and this toy is cheap but I was not pleased with the edges where the plastic has been cut out so the cat can reach their paw in to get the ball.  I think their fur probably protects their legs but the plastic edges are somewhat crude and can scratch human skin.  The toy is well designed in that the ball has not gotten out even though our dog has had a go at it as well.

Our cat likes to play with this toy. It's not his favorite toy, but he seems to like it. The downside is that it's lightweight and the cat just flips the whole thing. In the middle of the night, that's pretty terrifying.

My human bought me this thinking I would be interested. I'm not. I'd much rather hiss and screech at the outside cats that have the nerve to get close to my territory.This was a lot more inviting when my human would sprinkle catnip on/around it but she's getting old and senile. She put the catnip away and promptly forgot where. So...this sits on the floor and the only time I pay any attention to it is when Human bats the ball around the circle herself. I watch then because it's fun to see her make a giant fool of herself.There are lots of cats that evidently like this kind of thing but I find it utterly boring. I gave it three stars because it seems to be pretty well made.

I LOVE this thing. i have 5 cats, and they shed like crazy. all i do is rub in circles, and the hair balls up so i can throw it away, or on the floor to vacuum up later. haven't had to wash it yet, and i use it every day. recommend this to anyone who has pets that shed.

I have a shelter of cats and this is the best hair remover I have ever known, it works perfect. By mistake I asked for the other product that looks similar: Gonzo, but the  Magic Pet Hair Remover  is just superior! you can wash it, let it dry and go on using it a thousand times!!! I am very happy to have a clean place, thanks to Four Paws!.

I was on the phone and the pup felt ignored. She took this into her bed and chomped it into bits in just a few minutes. Not for strong chewers. She's not particularly mouthy, though she does seem to have a generalized hatred of leashes. Still, this is the only one she's sliced up into bits, so I can't recommend it for larger breeds since I hardly got any use out of it before it was snacked on.

I really like this lead for walking my 6 month old Black Lab.  Believe it or not,  my pup likes to be on a lead!  However, my husband mistakenly tied the pup out with this lead and pup chewed it apart in about five places.  Since it is cotton and he loves to chew, the lead was destroyed.This is my second lead like this one and he has destroyed both.  I suppose I am too organized, to have a lead for walking and a different type one for putting pup outside, and then to hope they would be used that way. Just proves, we don't live in a perfect world.  Sorry if I sound upset, I really am.  I really like this lead and it would have worked well for me.  I had it all of one day and didn't even get to use it.  If you have a dog that chews, be watchful.  Otherwise, it is a great lead.  It is not the lead's fault it gets chewed up!Would recommend otherwise.
teaching my pup with and e collar and this works great.it leave some room to walk without letting the dog run away

I use this one for my Shiba puppy to practice recall outside. It is a great training tool for dogs that don't heel very well and can't be off leash. This leash looks very promising for the spring and summer. It's too long now because it drags in the snow and slush faster than I can wrap it around my hand. This is not a fault of the product, which is well-made, just poor timing on my part.

wasn't sure on size so ordered both a 1 and zero for a yorkie. The zero is best for my little 8lb guy, but my 20lb fella needed the 1. They are strong and did the job.

I suppose my cocker spaniel is a small one. He is full grown. This muzzle covered his whole face. I don't have the package to send it back. I just have to cut it down to size and resew it to fit him. It came within a weeks time frame. So the vender was good about that. It looks like it is leather, but it isn't. It is a black vinyl.
As a professional dog trainer I found this to be a great product at a great price. Buy with confidence.

This stuff is very thick, so be sure to have cotton swabs on hand to put this on the wounds.  It is very thick (thicker than honey), and it will cling to any fur or hair along the way. My cat has a tumor on his ear and it was growing faster than normal  I used this Gel on the areas that needed dressing.Fortunately, it was just for a day or so and it stopped growing.  The Gel helped protect the area on his ear.  I didn't have to take him back to the vet for this situation.I am glad I have this on hand.

Yes , according with strong comments by others buyers , we're feeling into a Peace of Mind situation shopping an useful/practical/efficient/strong product as above ... Hoping it could help the Treasure of my Life by wounds issues asap ...
This is a nice quality dog bed. It fit perfectly in the collapsible dog travel box I purchased separately. I'm pretty sure my dog would recommend this also.

It's no thicker than a standard fleece crate pad. An inch to two thick. The pad flattened out (broke in) fairly quickly. I'd like something a little cushier for my 70 lb. dog. That said I'll credit it for construction. It's made decently. Materials are good. If a regular crate pad is what you want then this is a pretty good pad at the price.

It fits perfectly in most standard size crates and is a good thickness - not overly puffy for inside a crate, but enough stuffing to actually provide some cushioning.  When I have used thinner mats, they just slip around and get folded up, but this stays put pretty well.  Super easy to wash and retains its shape.  It also seems pretty durable - my dog scratches pretty hard when he's making his bed and there are no tears.

I got these to go on my dogs coolaroo beds inside. They are so much easier to keep clean than the zip covers on foam beds.  If the dogs bring in grass, dirt clods etc it just takes a minute to shake them outside.  They wash and dry quickly and there is no struggle to put them on.  The dogs seem to like them and scrunch them up the way they want them to be.
I bought two. One for my foldable travel crate and one for my regular crate. My German Shepherd loves it. You can flip it over depending on the weather, for a more cosy or cool feel. Nice!
The bed is soft and nice looking. My dog chewed it up in about 10 minutes so I never got to find out if it's durable after washing.
This is a good quality mat, the construction is tough - I have a chewer!It doe snot provide much support, though.

Bought this for my small dog for inside his crate. It fit well in the crate and he was comfortable on it. Washed it a couple times and it held up well after washes. He doesn't use a crate anymore so we moved it to inside his big bed in the bedroom and he still loves it.

It's a great idea as one side is for winter, and one side is for summer! It's also the perfect size to put in a crate. The denim bed is also useful as it doesn't get dirty easily and is easy to wash when our puppy has accidents.

We purchased this bed to go in a dog crate, and while it works sufficiently, and it is well-made, it is on the thin side - kind of like a very old, used, flat pillow, and that just isn't quite what we were hoping for, hence the  okay  rating.  If that's all you're looking for, then great - this is for you!
This bed seems to stand the test of time - I have it in his crate and he hasn't ripped it to shreds yet
It's a very nice crate pad, but I would not go far enough to call it a dog bed.I was expecting a thicker padding for being called a  bed.

This is a very well made bed with super soft fleece side. I haven't had it long enough to wash it yet so not sure how it will hold up. Seeing as how the stitching is good and tight I expect it will wear well and wash well. Some reviews said it didn't have enough padding. Id say that it is a really nice comfortable bed for a crate, where you dont want a real thick padding, and for a small dog would be fine for a regular bed. My two Puppies just love this bed, they always lie on it and seem to be very happy with it.

I bought this to go in my dog's crate, but it's since become his bed/snack spot (he drags his bones there to eat them...)I love it. Absolutely love it! Then into the dryer it goes, and puppy loves it!
This is a very nice cushy dog bed.  I like that you can reverse it for the seasons.  Our lab has some arthritic problems, but he gets hot laying on most dog beds.  Not this one! He loves it.
We use this on our dogs and never get fleas or anything so I guess it's working!! I hate that it's so expensive but I will continue to buy it.

Have used this for many years in central Maine on 5 different dogs, and it's been flawless.  Never had a flea or a tick, and that's on dogs that are outside 14 hours a day in large fenced yard, with lots of shrubs, bushes and grasses for bugs to hide on.  Lasts the full 30 days as stated, and is easy to apply, with no smell.  Love it!
We used this for years but the fleas in this area no longer are affected by it. We had to go to the Tritack to control the fleas in this area.

This is the best flea control you can buy for your dog.  Trust me when I say,  DON'T BE CHEAP WHEN IT COMES TO FLEAS!   Yes, it is kinda expensive, but worth it.  My dogs get a severe case of the fleas every year.  This stuff works the best.  I have tried almost everything out there, but this did the trick.

I live in the Midwest & flea season is always bad here. This works well. I have collies & they are known to be sensitive to many drugs and I have had no adverse reactions of any kind. I also have 2 tiny poms & it works well on them. Not much else I can say it works and I use it on everything from puppies to my big dogs.

I thought for the price this would be good. It didn't work. It would go off sometimes when the other dog barked that didn't have it on and sometimes it wouldn't go off at all with the dog that had it on barking. I had to send it back.
This collar does work and is nice that the levels can be adjusted.  Only problem is being outside every time the barking starts as consistency is key to training.

i am an animal lover and not a big fan of these kind of products however when it came down to trying this or having to get rid of the dog i opted for this. took 1 bark and 1 shock. i took it off of her and now i only have to show it to her if she starts barking for no reason. dogs are suppose to bark at certain things so i don't think you need to keep it on the dog all the time. most dogs learn quickly and this did the trick for my dog. also my dog is a 50 lb american bulldog and this fit with no problem.

This has sure changed things around our house.  Have a young cocker spaniel who is the light of my life, but her barking was driving me to distraction.  It only took a few days and she understood she had to be 'Quiet'.  I only put it on her now when I'm going to be working from home and don't want any barking. The first time she started a barking frenzy, at about the third big bark she jumped.  But, she didn't fall over and die and I was certain was going to happen - so all is well.  If you have barking issues - this is definitely the purchase to make.

I have not used this collar yet because there is something missing in the package....... a battery. I ordered the sometimes bought together package. I went back and looked at it and the numbers on those batteries are different from the ones indicated in the instruction manual. Apparently, this company does not include a battery to start you off. If the bought together batteries are incorrect, I will be very angry.
All it took was one time putting this on my goldendoodle and she stopped barking instantly.  She immediately connected the vibration to the barking.  Only wish I had purchased this ages ago.

I've order other cheaper brands.This one actually works longer than a week. It's very easy to use. It emits a sound to warn the dog that the shock is about to happen. It took one time and our dog has stopped barking when people come to the door. It stopped our 2nd dog from barking too. If 2nd dog does bark once, the collar won't go off on the dog with collar on. We take it off when people are not coming over and at night. It's not too bulky or heavy for our small 12 pound dog. We just cut the long collar length. This bark collar works well but in order to shut it off you have to remove the battery. The battery itself is not made that well that it can stand repeated removals.
my dog is not barking anymorei dont know exacly how is workingbut is workinggood product for you

One of my dogs was an obsessive barker who didn't take notice to my manual corrections. This collar helped me out by giving him a correction nick and got more intense when he didn't response to the low level correction. My dog responded well with this collar and within couple training sessions of use his excess barking is under control.

Ok, so none of us want to shock our little buddy.  But if hes as obnoxious as my chihuahua was..he has to be taught some manners.  You wouldn't let you kid scream every time someone came to the door, and continue screaming throughout their visit..so you have to think of it as DISCIPLINE.  And believe me, they learn FAST.  Do you think youll have to make Fido endure this collar forever?  You wont.  Keep it on him till he puts himself in the position of getting a little shock two times.  He wont be a happy camper.  Say  No Bark!  or  QUIET!  when he gets a  zap.  (Its mild, it just scares the h*** out of them).  Then, take the collar off.  Next time he starts to bark inappropriately, give the command and hold the collar up for him to see.  With my dog..thats all it took for him to completely change his attitude.  Hes now a little gentleman  when company comes to the door.  He'll still bark..but when I say  No Bark!  he stops.  I don't even have to show him the collar anymore.If you have a stubborn dog..you will need to give him a refresher course now and them.  This is a GREAT training tool.  Don't buy one of these collars with the idea of leaving it on continuously.  A dogs gotta bark sometimes.  Hes protecting you and his domain.  You don't want a fearful, neurotic dog.  It may not solve the problem completely..but youll see a huge improvement..and your friends will start coming to visit you again!

We have a tweenie lang-haired dachshund (17lbs) who can't resist barking at the beagle next door (that never shuts up). We got this collar from my in-laws who tried it on their dog with no success. We figure, hey free bark collar, let's try it.We could never figure out if our dog ever really got zapped by the collar. When we practiced with it, we could never get it to light up or shock anything. We thought, perhaps it was just that our dog hated wearing it and was shamed into not barking? We scratched it up pretty bad and bent it trying to get it open but never succeeded. We thought, well perhaps our dog won't notice (he did) and he will still stop barking when wearing it (he does). The company I bought it from listed this one but they actually sent the newer model. I wanted the older one, but it was no big deal really. The highest setting does work on our Great Dane but it slacks in his skin sometimes so a couple more levels (such as in the old one) might have helped.Other than that, these are great training devices and when used correctly I have found are only needed for a short time.

Have used this system for 8 years with my dogs and it works very well. We have the PetSafe In-Ground fence and it works really well for our lab.  We inherited another dog and needed to add a collar to our system.  We bought this and it arrived very quickly and in perfect working order.  Right now, we have it in beep-only mode while we start the first week of her training.  Hopefully you can teach an old dog new tricks!

Just like all the petsafe products, great quality. Put the battery in and good to go. I remove the device and drill holes in another (metal free) collar and attach the device. That way you get to use the device but have a better looking collar.

I now have 2 of these (bought approx. 1 year apart).  They both work great, and I turned one all the way up (VERY easy to do) for one of my dogs.  They do just what they're meant to do, and I have no complaints.

Bought this for my finches but they go check it out and fly off without so much as a bite.  I threw some out to the pigeons and not even they will eat it  Wasted my money.

Well, our dog loves a snake, anything he can shake and conquer.  Our other dog loves to run around with anything long. When I take the squeakers out, the dogs like it more, but there seems to be something about the face (or maybe the memory of the squeak) that startles both dogs. Stopped my dog with separation anxiety from barking after 2 barks. My landlord threatened to make me get rid of my dog or move but this thing saved me. Highly recommended.

Somebody said that this product works for a small dog. Too big for my Chihuahua. Plus she figured out how to loosen the belt and get it off her neck. So useless on two fronts.Why not make a smaller one for small dogs??
This didn't work on my barking Pom. He just kept barking & didn't miss a beat. I let a friend use it for her dog & it didn't work on him either.

I bought 6 bags of this for my 100 gallon aquarium. I followed all instructions, first pouring in the substrate into tank, then slowly filling it with de-chlorinated water per instructions (I dechlorinated water inside a brute 40-gallon tank and used a submersible pump to move this dechlorinated water into my aquarium). The first thing you will notice is that the package is vaccum sealed and contains about 2 cups of water (in addition to the substrate) which holds beneficial bacteria, which is why it is necessary to use dechlorinated water.I took off 1/2 star because the contents of the package was extremely foul smelling. Since I bought 6 packages, my living room became extremely smelly, it smells like a sewer. This is the most foul smelling substrate I have ever bought, but if it's good for my plants, then I'm willing to deal with that. After 4 days, the foul smell is finally gone. I do not know if fish can be added to the tank while the water is still foul smelling but it takes a few weeks to properly nitrogen cycle the tank anyway. I would not add this substrate to an established tank that already contains fish, given that the substrate smell can penetrate water and evaporate into air in order to be smelled. Other reviewers did not comment in this 4 day duration of foul odor, but my case may be severe because I used 6 bags for my 100 gallon tank.I took of 1/2 star because the substrate clouds the water a lot, which is more noticeable in larger aquariums. I trickled the dechlorinated water onto a large family size salad bowl while filling the aquarium with water, at a rate of about 1 gallon per 5 minutes, to prevent disturbance of the substrate. After my aquarium was filled, the water was a very cloudy yellow grey brown, with visibility of approximately 5 inches. I ran my Fluval FX6 canister filter and my AquaClear 110 HOB filter simultaneously (both of which have 5 micron filter floss water polisher media from http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B0046UXMY6/ref=ox_sc_sfl_title_2?ie=UTF8&psc;=1∣=A1YTQUKKLAHTT7), making sure the filter output was not disturbing the substrate. After 24 hours of dual filtration, I saw very little improvement in cloudiness (visibility improved to approximately 6 inches), so I drained the cloudy water (about 95 gallons worth) and filled it again. This time the water was much less cloudy and visibility is about 24 inches. This substrate is actually much less cloudy than 4 other competing aquarium plant substrates that I have tried. All other substrates needed to be washed at least 10 times to even reach this level of water clarity. I am just disappointed that the manufacturer claims that this substrate does not have to be rinsed, when it could really use two or three washes.

Here's the thing: You need to use a LOT of litter to make this box work well, and if your cat is a good squatter (ours are, neither stands and lets fly), it works great. But put in a good 3-4  of litter. Sure, it seems deep, but if you consider that the peeing-area of this box is a lot smaller than it seems (because of the curved bottom), it really does not use any more litter than a big flat one.This dome litter box works best if you clean it REGULARLY. Size does matter.  When it comes to filter bags.  Most filter bags are too large to properly fit in the filter box of the small Aquaclear 20/Aquaclear Mini power filter.  Most media bags are designed to be used with a canister filter.  However, this filter bag is the exception since it was designed specifically for the Aquaclear 20.  There are also filter media bags that are specifically designed for the larger Aquaclear filters.Having this bag allows you to pack your own carbon rather than buying the prepackaged Aquaclear carbon.  It can save you a little bit of money in the long run if you buy carbon in bulk quantities.  However, the biggest benefit that I have experienced is that you will have the option to try different brands of carbon.  Carbons are not all equal.  While the Aquaclear carbon does a good job of keeping the water in the fish tank odorless, it is not very good at removing tannins from mopani wood.  The best carbon for that task, in my experience, is the Matrix brand from a company called Seachem.  It does cost more than other carbon brands so you end up not saving money compared to just buying the AC prepackaged carbon.  I suppose the option you choose will depend on what you are trying to remove from the water.There is a temptation to fill the bag completely when packing your own carbon.  However, you will get better performance if you pack loosely and leave a lot of room.  For example, you can easily pack more than 5 tablespoons of carbon in this bag.  But if  you do that, the water will not flow through all of the carbon in the bag.  The key to efficient use of carbon media is to allow water to flow through all of it and preferably at a slow rate.  The design of the typical power filter works against this because they compensate for efficiency (filtration thoroughness) with volume.  In other words, not all of the water is cleaned thoroughly at the first pass.  But by passing the water through multiple times in a short amount of time, you eventually trap most of the debris.  This is why a canister filter with a much slower rate of flow can outperform a power filter.  The canister filter will allow for less water by-pass.  What this means to you as a power filter user is that you will be passing your water through your filter media at a comparatively faster flow rate.  You would want to make sure that your carbon is not packed too tightly or the water will simply go around the bag.  Pack less carbon, but change out more often.Carbon is not the only chemical media that you can put in the bag.  Zeolite and peat are two items that you can use if you want to adjust your water.  Peat removes carbonate hardness and adds tannins in the water.  Some people actually like that yellow tint to the water.  And some fish species may prefer it.  Zeolite can help get ammonia under control in an emergency situation.  Just be sure that whatever you want to use is not small enough to escape the bag.  Some resins are too small to be contained in this bag.

This bubble ladder is pretty big.  It measures about 10 inches tall, by about 4 inches wide, and about 3/4 of an inch thick.  Takes up a fair amount of room in a 10 gallon tank.  It comes with three black suction cups, two attach to the top, and one to the bottom.If you are running DIY CO2, bubble ladders are nice due to the low pressures needed to operate.  A diffuser will dissolve a larger proportion of CO2 into the water, but require much high pressures to operate - particularly once they start to get dirty.

As noted by other reviewers.  It takes about 24 hours for the bubbles to completely ascend the ladder.  Now they ascend and I can see them get smaller as they rise.I would start with  the yeast specified in recipes.  I used full amount and was getting way to many bubbles.  I ended up dumping  the solution out to reduce the bubble count.  Not sure if it would have calmed down but did not want to asphyxiate my fish.  You can always add more yeast later.

Using this bubble counter lets you see large carbon dioxide bubbles become progressively smaller as they move up the ladder.  Plant growth changes, improving, sometimes flourishing.  Not all species of plants respond the same'  some grow well, some hardly at all.  This item  can be used with DIY carbon dioxide producers (yeast, sugar) so for just a few dollars any hobbyist who wants to improve their growth of fresh water tropical plants.  Their documentation says that this is good for tanks up to 20 gallons, although it also functions well in a 55 gallon sun-lit tank where constant pruning of a couple of hardy species is a regular job.Pros:  low cost, can be used with DIY systems, actually improves plant growth, it's cool to see the bubbles get smaller as they rise (approx 1 per sec,depending on state of CO2 producer)cons:  limit to how big of a tank it can be used for (they claim 20 gal),  sometimes needs to be cleaned of slime/algae

The best stand-alone aquarium thermometer I have owned.  It is much better than the old fashioned kind.  Very accurate, and is easy to read.

Bought this and installed it in my 29H aquarium on January 5, 2014. I was using a glass thermometer and wanted something easier to read.This thermometer works well, but the accuracy needs to be checked. My old thermometer read about 2F lower than the Coralife Digital thermometer.To check to see which was correct (never doubted the temperature readings on the old one) the thermometers needed to be checked in ice water.I filled a glass with ice and water and mixed it up.  I placed both thermometers in the ice water and waited 10 minutes before checking the temperature reading of each thermometer.After 10 minutes my old glass thermometer was reading just above the 32F mark.  The Coralife Digital thermometer was reading 33.5F. My Coralife thermometer is reading 1.5F higher than the actual temperature.The suction cup to hold the thermometer on the aquarium did not work at first.  It was deformed from the packaging. To fix this I boiled some water and poured it over the suction cup in a dish. I left the suction cup in the hot water for a few minutes then removed it with a spoon. I carefully massaged it back into shape and it works just fine. Prior to this the suction cup fell off every 3 minutes.This means I must subtract 1.5F from the reading.I would recommend checking the thermometer in ice water before trusting the displayed reading.  The instructions say it's accurate to +/- 1.5F. If yours is off more,  I would consider exchanging it.Recommended: yes,  but must be checked in ice water for accuracy.
