I use it on my Australian Shepherd.  Excellent brush for removing dead fur.

My dog loves the tricky treat ball! It is just about his favorite toy to eat from. The only draw back is it is difficult to clean (as in almost impossible to effectively get in there and wash it). My dog, a big chewer, does not chew this. He rolls it around, and then carries it around the house for about an hour. It's very cute.
The pup absolutely loves this ball...treats drop out randomly and slowly and the pup has not been able to tear it up.

The dogs all like this, it is a handy size, perfect for playing games and the texture makes it easy for all sizes of dogs to use.  There is no odor, it is durable and something we will buy for friends with pets too.
Have a GSD and she is loves to chew....this toy is not only strong, it provides her with hours of entertainment.  Definitely worth the price...one of the best purchases I ever made for my dog!

I got this toy for my golden mix puppy when she was only a couple of months old and it worked to keep her occupied until she got all of the treats out. However last month (at ll months old) the pup figured out that the easiest way to get the treats out would be to sink her teeth into one of the  grab  holes, and make a much bigger hole than the one provided. Another toy bites the dust. All we have left are bones. Sigh.....
only problem is that it rolls under the sofa and tables.  I have started leaving it in the kitchen and that works much better

I got two large balls for my two large dogs and it's so funny to watch them bat, nudge and try to get treats out.  This thing is a lifesaver when it's rainy out or the weather is crappy in general.  Our 7 month old puppy is a little more high energy than our 3 year old and you could keep filling this up with dry food and he'd be at it for hours.  I highly suggest for boredom or just to entertain yourself with. ;)

My puppy loves this ball for eating his dinner! It's challenging, so it takes him about 20 minutes to eat 3/4 cup of kibble. You have to train them to eat out of toys, so don't be surprised if the dog just stares at it in the beginning. My puppy caught on pretty quickly though. I started him on this at 4.5 months.

I'm not sure if this was a three or four stars toy. It lasted a long time, a few months, with no damage or issue. Treats went in ball, dog rolled ball, dog got treats, hurray!But then dog wanted to get all the treats, all at once. So dog bit the ball, and bit it some more. He got a really good grip on it because of all the indents, and the ball just collapsed. Shattered is probably more appropriate. It was totally unusable after that, and dog is a clever enough beast that I think he would break the next one in short order.Works well until the dog figures out that biting it might work. And it does.

A smart dog is a boon unless he has insufficient entertainment. In which case, he will find his own entertainment and it may involve the evisceration of a decorative pillow and the defecating of polyfill a day or two later. This Tricky treat ball, on the other hand, is fun for everyone. There is one tube opening into the ball's hollow center you can fill with small food or treats. It only doles out kibble when rolled just right. The more kibble inside, the more will fall out but it becomes more challenging as it empties and my teacup mastiff Anchovy, loves to work out every last bite on his own. He will also go and find it when I'm busy and boring. I laugh aloud to see him trot off and return with the orange ball in mouth, drop it and nose it around the room, gobbling up whatever he manages to roll out of it. He paws and bats it, too.It's a simple but challenging toy that rewards a dog for playing with it and that's earned Anchovy's highest rating, four out of four paws.

Awesome toy. My lab couldnt care less about it but my Rottweiler rolls it all over the house, down the stairs, outside in the yard. My lab did learn to pick it up and bounce it to get the treats out....but this toy is really the rotties. I also bought one for my Dad's toy poodle and he loved it too.

We bought the 3  one from petco a while back, used the heck out of it with our 20lb pup. She LOVED IT! Finally almost a year later she tore the tube inside which blocks the treats from just falling out. So we bought this one. It surprisingly has a smaller hole than the 3  one...and the only treat that goes in and out are her kibble. Anything bigger gets stuck. Im going to get the 3  one like we used to have, but this one may work better for someone with a big dog.

I always prefer toys that are stimulating and this one is. I fill it with Zukes minis and my dogs roll it all over gods creation trying to get them out. You can fill it with kibble too. It is not a chew toy and I assume if dogs started chewing it would probably not last long. Unless your dog is really dumb just show them to roll it and treats come out and they'll catch on real quick.
Just too easy.  I prefer the iq ball.  This really pours out food. The dog does play with it when filled with food.  It's also quiet on hard floors compared to the dogs hard plastic feeding toys.

This was ripped within 5 minutes. Costco had the larger version and my sister got it for her hound. He loves it and it keeps him occupied. This one is small and soft.I have only purchased KONG and Nylabone products in the past and will continue to do so in the future. Lesson learned.Would I buy it again? No way.If you have a very small, inactive-ish, dog this might work for you.

This treat ball is great. My dog loves playing with it (probably hates it but he wants the treats inside). I usually put a lot of treats in it so they come out a little more frequently, I dont want my dog to get too frustrated with it. With the amount of treats I put it in it (I use broken up mini-milk bones he seems fine with it), enough of a payout for the work and it keeps him occupied for 10-15 minutes at a time.The downside to this toy (why I knocked off a star) is that it originally had a VERY strong plastic smell. So strong that my dog wouldn't use it. Maybe 3 weeks/month after I put it out for him he has really started using it which is good, but it took that long for the smell to wear off enough for him to use it. It still has a detectable odor if you're near it but its a fraction of what it began as.This ball is durable. My dog usually tears right through toys (even without the incentive of a treat inside) but this ball has held up well so far, I see no tears or breaks.Glad I gave this to my buddy!

My 8 mth old GR loves this as it's much easier than the other treat dispensing toys that we have at home. I like it as it's quiet on my tile floors and the only grievance is that sometimes he doesn't finish all the kibble inside so I have to shake it rather violently to get them out for him. Its also quite a pain to wash and to remove all the water inside. There's this lovely vanilla scent as mentioned by other reviewers and the rubber is rather soft. Luckily my puppy hasn't taken to biting or chewing it as I showed him that he only needs to nudge it with his nose or paws to get it rolling before his kibble falls out. He is also not interested in it once there's very little kibble left. However, it would be wise to be careful as this can get shredded to pieces if your dog is a chewer!

I use this treat ball as a feeding device for my dog. I put her dinner in the ball and when it gets down to the last few pieces we play soccer with the ball. It is easy for her to pick it up and drop it (she's an English Springer Spaniel).

I've tried a number of these treat balls, hoping our dachshund would get some indoor exercise this winter.. This one sounds like it's a smart way to go, but he won't play with it and I don't like it.. It has a really strong plastic odor and when I put treats inside of it, they don't come out easily.. I would think any dog would get bored with trying to get something out of it, IF you can get them to play with it at all.. Our Champie just sniffs it, then walks away.. I think the plastic odor probably covers the scent of the treat inside, so he's not even interested in it... I tried washing it in hot soapy water, but it didn't get rid of the smell... Plus it took forever to get all the water out of it and get it to dry.. Maybe more playful dogs would enjoy this, or maybe bigger dogs, but for our little guy, he just isn't interested. Waste of money!

I bought this because the other reviews said their dogs played with it for hours. I was hoping for something to help alleviate boredom in my dog on rainy days or especially high active days. I honestly didn't expect any toy to occupy her attention for hours (though it would have been nice!). She definitely played with it several times during the day when there were treats inside but instead of rolling the ball to get the treats to fall out, she figured she might as well chew a bigger hole in the ball and fish the treats out herself. So now the ball is somewhat useless.I think for a dog that won't destroy it, it may be a much more worthwhile purchase. Since my dog can chew through anything (kong toys included) this lasted literally 2 days before it went to the recycle bin.

This toy gets chewed on almost daily and is still in great condition, my pup usually destroys things, but this one is still going strong! The hole is smaller so she really has to work for it! I would recommend.

This is a great way to engage your dog in mealtime or playtime. Most of the time, my dog is  take it or leave it  with regard to toys, so if I need to keep her occupied (when I'm working from home/ cleaning my apartment/ entertaining), this is great. The ball holds about 1/3 cup of food (or treats if you want) and can keep her going for up to 15 minutes. The one gripe I have with this is that the sticky texture does attract hair, but that's more of a commentary on my own inability to stay on top of her shedding! I put it in the top rack of my dishwasher and it came out fine, so it's not TOO much of an issue. All in all, this is a unique and fun way to feed (or play with) your dog!
My dog loves pushing this thing around. It dispenses treats at a nice rate. Keeps her busy for a good 10-15 minutes.

I bought this because our dog broke the last treat dispensing ball that we bought.  That one came apart in two pieces to load the treats and was an excellent toy…until he broke it open and started eating the plastic itself!I bought this one as a replacement because it doesn't come apart like the other one so he can't break it open and eat the ball itself.  So far, he's loving it!  The kibble and/or treat pieces aren't terrible difficult to get out, but it does take him a little while (long enough to give us break from him pushing toys on our laps for a bit!).  I recommend this treat ball.Our dog is a 50 lb collie mix and can fit the entire ball in his mouth, for reference.
My dog tore this to pieces with an hour

This treat ball is an active-dog owner's best friend. My dog loves to roll it all over the house. He'd much rather eat his dinner from the treat ball than from his bowl! The best thing about it, for me, is that it is almost silent. It's a soft rubber, so there is no clatter or crashing. I used to have a hard plastic cube, but that made a huge racket on the wooden floor, which my dog loved but I hated.It's easy to fill (I use a small funnel), easy to spot in a dark corner or under a chair because it's bright orange, and my little dog can pick it up and carry it around. He's a 12-pound maltese, so the ball comes up about to his chest, and he bats it with his paws and pushes it with his snout, which is extremely cute.I've had it for about 6 months and it is as good as new with daily use. I got another one for my sisters' larger dog, and she loves it, too.

Excellent product. Worth every penny.  My Alaskan Malamute LOVES this.  He knocks it around and throws it to see how much kibble he can get out of it.  He will even throw it to me when he needs a refill.  My dog devours his food and since he is a large breed I worry about bloat.  So I put his dinner in the ball and he takes his time eating it SLOWLY.  If your dog likes to chew on balls, there are better products for that.  This is more for using their paws and we love it!!

My bully mix took a couple days of interactive play to understand how it worked (no need to destroy it to get the food).  If left alone with it, she'll chew on it and she could definitely rip it apart.  I use it for her meals, now that she's learned how it works, and then take it away.  It's much quieter than the atomic treat ball, which is chew-proof.

My dogs love this--I put plain Cheerio's in it and despite them chewing on it to try to get the Cheerio's out, they haven't done any more than some surface damage.  Great toy that keeps them entertained.

My dog took a long time to warm up to this ball and then the first time she got really into it she ended up chewing it into pieces.  It is really hard to get treats out of this ball.  The first time I gave it to her, she got so frustrated that she completely gave up and even I had a really hard time getting the treats out (which makes it hard to clean as well).  Finally, she got the hang of it one day with some marrow bites, but in order to get the last few she just decided to chew through it.  I'm giving it 4 stars anyway because it explicitly says to start with smaller treats that are easier to get out so your dog won't get frustrated (woops) and because it isn't meant for aggressive chewers.  If your dog is a normal chewer this would be a great toy.

Great Toy. Physically and mentally stimulating. We are constantly trying to come up with new ways to challenge our German Shepherd. She is often too smart for her own good! Prior to getting this ball we used to take her food and scatter it around on the floor requiring her to move around, sniff it out and find it. This ball is another clever way to feed your dog. As they nudge the ball around food comes out in small amounts. Perfect form of entertainment and stimulation. Highly recommended.

We have a puppy Vizsla and he needs a lot of attention and stimulation. This was a great puzzle game for him. We just put some kernels of dog food in there and let the play time begin... entertaining for us to watch too.
I order this and another puzzle toy for my pups. This is a great toy and seems pretty durable so far. The main issue I have with this is it can not be cleaned easily.

I bought this for my newly adopted Maltese-mix who had no idea how to play.  My poodle has this and Ms. Beatrice became intrigued, but wasn't quite sure about it.  Once the treat ball arrived, I immediately filled it with some treats and kibble.  It took her a little while to figure out how to roll the ball to get the treat.  Now, whenever both my girls see I have their treat balls, they are so excited.  I give them to them right when I'm leaving the house and I no longer exist! :)  They are also great to use when the girls are just way too rambunctious.  They act like  pacifiers .  By they time they've rolled all the treats out, they sufficiently tuckered out and usually take a nap.  It's just so rough being a dog! :D
I probably need to spend some time with them teaching them about the food inside but so far, after 3 months, they don't even bother with these. Now my mom's dog loves hers so depends on the dog.
My Straffordshire Terrier destroyed this within a short time.  This won't work for dogs who like to chew, not durable enough.

My dog enjoyed rolling and bouncing this around to get some treats. She caught on quickly and it entertained her for about 10 minutes at a time. It lasted for about 4 months but ultimately she tore it apart. It was worth the price.
I bought this for my bichon and feed him all his meals of dry food in this. Because it takes him while to get the food out of the ball, he eats slower and seems more satisfied.

My 90 lb lab/shepherd? mix (the question mark is for his tail that curls over his back with an end that is practically prehensile) loves the toy.  Ordinarily he demolishes his toys but this one he adores and carries it around with him.  I put a few of the really small trainer treats in the ball and that kept him rolling the ball around with his nose or paws for some time but he really likes to carry it around with him.  It is soft enough for him to carry it easily in his mouth.

I got this for my ball loving dog. In less than 5 minutes of receiving the box and getting it out of the packaging there was a hole torn in it. He isn't the type of dog to destroy anything. The ball has a smell to it of vanilla or some sort that must have made him destroy it. Looks like only Chuck-it balls from here on out. A definite waste of money.
Perfect size for a few small bowls for 2 mischievous kittens. Keeps any spillages within bounds courtesy of the raised edges.
Have bought three so far.  I spray it inside with Lysol with every scooping.  So that the cup won't smell and so that their fur doesn't pick up bacteria while in there touching the sides.

I was very skeptical at first as to how this litter box worked,  self cleaning , without a motor, electricity etc. I was also skeptical due to the price being far less then other  self cleaning  litter boxes. Well, let me tell you, I am now a believer! Lol. No, seriously this litter box does exactly what it says. You literally roll the box to the right, then back to the left and then remove the tray that now contains any and all kitty excretions! It was more then simple to put together, just place the grate in the box, add litter, snap on the top, and slide in the tray and your kitty is free to do his business. Took me about 10 mins total to figure out how to put it together and also how to use it! But this is only because I put the grate in backwards and thus prevented it from functioning properly. After I YouTube  how to use the Omega self-cleaning litter bow  I found a video made by the actual inventor of this wonderful box and 4 minutes later I had the grate in correctly and was good to go. It's been almost 3 weeks since we started using the box. I have one medium size grey tabby and he had no problem transitioning at all. In fact, he used it within 10 mins of me putting it together  (probably out of curiosity) we have had no issues and it now takes me literally 1 minute to roll the box, take out the tray and throw out the goods. There is less smell, less mess, and less litter on my floor around the box because of the lid. The only recommendation I would give is to make sure you buy the right size box. I bought the medium and although my cat has no problems fitting in it I think the large would have been a bit more roomy for him so when I buy my next Omega box I will go up a size. Because my next box WILL be another one of these! Thank you guy who invented this simple but perfect litter box!

I love these litter boxes. I have one large one and got this smaller one for another part of the house. Our cats adore these litter boxes. They love their privacy. One of my cats is rather large and I didn't think he would fit, but he makes it work. It almost looks like he's getting into a clown car, but it's roomy enough inside for him to use it without any issues so I'm happy :)My main suggestion is to use a GOOD clumping litter that won't break apart when you roll the box over to clean it. I used to use fresh-step litter but had issues with it clumping the Pee, so I switched to the recommended band of Amazon: Precious Cat Ultra Premium Clumping Cat Litter. My cats LOVE this litter and I do to!

The medium box has held together better but still a couple of the clips that hold it shut do not work or are really tough to work.  The large was delivered broken, it was replaced with no hassle but the replacement box has not worked right from day one, it will not clip shut.  This box should have been designed with clips like those that are on other covered litter boxes rather than the ridiculous slide it into place and it never lines up right.  The box is a great concept, it works, roll it over and the clumps all go into the scoop, but make sure to pinch the box together in case the clips break or you will have a fine mess!
My 15lb cat uses this under protest, it really isn't big enough for him.  The 4lb kitten and 6lb female like it just fine.

Hard to clean, very messy because there isn't a door-so the litter goes everywhere.  I tried hooded, regular, special...you name it.  I still use it because I have 3 kittens, but I am going to get the Van Ness instead...

I love this item and we have several of them in our house.  Here are some other things worth mentioning:>> It's easy to clean - i.e., rolls like it says it does - and the used litter goes right into the pull out tray as it should.  To make it work the best, use a good quality litter which does clump really well.  (We were using Arm & Hammer because it was one of the cheapest on the market and found out it didn't clump very well. We switched to Fresh Step and the used litter is 99% captured with one roll.)>> There are two sizes: get the large one unless you have one really small cat.>> Some cats will not use this because it has a lid.  My cats range in size from petite to quiet large and only the two large, male cats really liked the cover.  (The minute I took the cover off, all the other cats used it as a regular little pan.  I simply put the lid back on when I wanted to clean it.)>> It will last for a long time.  Mine, on average, last about a year.  What ends up happening is that the plastic hooks that hold the top to the bottom break off.  DO NOT CONSIDER THIS AS A REASON NOT TO BUY ONE.  We put a lot of litter into ours so the wear and tear may be more than it's really designed for.  That's our issue - not a manufacturing problem.Take all the above into account and try one.  It's well worth the money.

I love things like this: no moving parts, hard to break, improves your life daily, simple, unmotorized, cheap.This box works great (although  self-cleaning  is a bit of a misnomer - you have to roll the box over, and roll it back, and then remove the waste that has collected in the little drawer) and keeps you from getting up close and personal with the dust/unpleasantness/etc of scooping a litter box.I will say, though, that you need litter that will clump EXTREMELY WELL. If the litter doesn't clump, the box doesn't work, period.I would highly suggest  Precious Cat Ultra Premium Clumping Cat Litter . Clumps really well, controls odor, and is mega cheap if you get it in the 40 pound bag. It's the best one I've found for this litter box so far.

My cat isn't a fan of boxes that are too enclosed, but since I'm moving & I have to put the litter box in my room, I much prefer a closed one. This one looked interesting from the videos. I put a piece of my cat's poop in it from the old litter, and after a few hours my cat used it!! And it really does work as advertised, even though the clips were tricky initially but doesn't take a genius to figure it out. I had to use scissors to cut a piece of plastic that was preventing it from clipping properly. When rolling the box, make sure to tip it beyond 90 degrees so you hear the thuds of ... stuff .. falling into the tray. I'm using Precious Cat Ultra Premium Clumping litter and that stuff is awesome. Someone at the shelter recommended it to me and it doesn't smell at all, and works really well with this box. A con - it also came with a long (but shallow) scratch but I figure it's from shipping, & I don't really mind.UPDATE:Some people say its too small, and it's really not that bad for my 12 lb long haired cat. The only problem was that once I noticed her tail was wet. When she goes closer to the grill, however, the litter does get stuck and I have to use a scoop still. But I have a small scoop that I keep in the tray so its still convenient.Some people have talked about waste of litter, but I really don't know what they're talking about! Clean litter doesn't fall into the tray and as long as you tip it back, it flows back into the main compartment. I only keep about 2 inches of litter in there and I clean it every 1 and a half days.

it's so clean and easy to use and assemble! i was skeptical at first when i first assembled it - would it really eliminate all hand scooping and sure enough, as long as the clumps are smaller than a tennis ball - you are good to go! just roll forward and then back and remove the scoop - so easy!

I literally love this thing. So does my kitty.  Probably gets cleaned more that it might have, had it been a regular cat box.  It's so easy and quick.  Didn't even take too long to figure it out.  Once put together, it seems very sturdy.  Depending on the size of your cat, you may opt for the larger one, but so far this works like a charm.  I would definitely recommend this to every cat owner.....

I have a Littermate in the house which is my third one and it just died today.  Outside, I have this one for the cats when they are out on the screen enclosed lanai.  I find this a whole lot easier to clean than the Littermate.  In fact I am replacing it with this one because I am tired of having to replace that one every few years!  My son is also very happy because cleaning out the littler boxes is his job and he hates cleaning the Littermate.  He's been wanting me to replace it with this one, but I needed to wait until it died.  I don't understand the low ratings from some reviewers because with two cats, I have never had an issue and have had this for several years.  That is why I am back for another one!  I highly recommend this product!

The only thing I DON'T like about this litter box is that the inside of the box is so much smaller than the outside due to the cleaning mechanism.  Thus I should have ordered a large for my small cat, and who knows what you do if you have a Maine Coon or something.  Anyway, the cat uses it so I must be the only one the tiny space bothers!  It's VERY easy for me to keep clean so I tend to clean it more often than my traditional one, although I do take the top off and comb it with the regular scoop from time to time as some of the smaller particles don't get caught up in the built-in cleaner.  Overall I would definitely buy it again and have recommended it to friends who are even more *ahem* forgetful than I am!

This product is wonderful. I use Tidy Cats clumping litter with it and it still works awesome. When I roll it I do hit the bottom, just to ensure the clumps fall. My cat is medium size (10-15lbs). While it is a bit cramped for her, she goes in it and turns around, and hasn't expressed any issues with it. The litter stays in the box which is an issue with most litter boxes I have had. I have had many automatic litter boxes. Perhaps the best feature is that it doesn't require electricity so it will never go out (like my $100+ box from Walmart). This product is so great I bought one for my mother's cats and she loves it also.

Got this today. Easy to set up. Love the concept. Easy to understand what to do.I'm gathering from the other reviews that this is literally the  cat's meow . Didn't giveit 5 stars as have not actually seen it through to a clean out yet. Thanks for this concept.How terrific!
The only thing better would be to teach them to use the toilet. But since that's not happening, this will do

This was worth -every- penny. We have it next to the toilet and I used Worlds Best Cat litter which is flushable. That combination makes me a HAPPY kitty owner. I just roll it, pull out the tray, and dump it in the toilet. DONE! Cat box is cleaned out once a day and I never touch anything! My 6/8lb kitties love it and I've never had any issues with them using it. One suggestion, don't roll it if there is wet waste - the grate is not easy to clean if you get waste stuck in it. Just let your kitty litter dry it out first.That is the only downside - the box isn't the easiest to clean (I do a deep clean 1x per month when i do a complete change of the litter). It's not that it's -difficult- to clean, it's just not as easy as a square pan. I think a few minutes of slightly-more-effort cleaning once a month is totally worth not having to scoop nasty waste though, so woohoo!If you have a cat, you need this. Period.

I even tried removing the lid and using it as a regular litter box.  The brand of litter makes all the difference.  I usually just picked up litter at the grocery when it was needed, as a result the box did not always remove the soiled litter.  I finally stumbled on Fresh Step clumping litter and it works like a charm now.  Only fresh litter remains in the box and I am not dumping lots of good litter when I clean.  This beats digging through dirty litter every time.

I'm updating this review because soon after I posted upon cleaning the litter box, I realized that I had installed the grated section incorrectly. This litter box works well to capture poo and urine clumps, but also seems to capture some clean litter. We are currently using Worlds Best Litter which seems to stick to the bottom of this box. Not sure if it's the box or the litter causing the sticking problem. Would like to hear how others have dealt with this issue.

Very pleased with how this turned out. I was a bit skeptical at first purchase, but it works exactly like it is supposed to. I use clumping litter, and every once in a while a urine clump will stick to the bottom, but a firm thump sends it into the bin with everything else with almost no effort, and no need for a litter scoop. Allows for extremely fast and easy cleaning.Also easily disassembled for monthly washing. Tabs seem a bit weak, but they have held so far with no issues.

This  regular  size isn't even big enough for our small cat to get in a turn around.  Probably would only be useful for kittens.  Most of the interior size is taken up by the disposal system.  I would HIGHLY recommend getting the large size for ANY size cat you have.  We knew when we put this one together, it wasn't going to work so we packed it right back up and are returning it.  We have ordered the larger one.  The system looks like a terrific idea and we are looking forward to getting the big one so see how large it really is.I was surprised that Prime, which ships for no charge and has allowed returns at no charge in the past is actually deducting the return shipping from my refund even though I am purchasing the bigger one....never had this happen before...change in Prime policy maybe?
This is the biggest rip-off device ever.  It doesn't work like it's supposed to and is just a hassle.  Clever TV marketing.  Sorry implementation.Don't do it.

I have had this about three weeks, Omega Paw replacing a fairly nice covered box of similar cost that lasted less than six months (hinges wore out, would not stay together, plastic split, etc) which entailed using a scoop to clean and keeping a minimum of 3 or 4 inches of litter at all times.Now for the new improved model:  OMEGA PAW:Does not need to be opened every time it is emptied, so no hinges to weaken.Works great with 2 to 3 inches of litter over a smaller area in bottom of box.The scoop is retired.The rolling feature works perfectly by rolling 3//4 turn slowly and tapping the bottom twice when in 3/4 roll position.Empty drawer into plastic grocery bag for disposal, and add 2 cups of litter (Precious Cat) about twice a week.Once a day is plenty of empties for our one adult cat.Incidentally, Picky-Picky took to it immediately.
This litter box was really nice at first, but after one or two times of changing the litter, the lid would NOT stay on and ended up getting litter everywhere every time it was time to change litter.

I have two cats and each is over 10 pounds.  I did not know if this would work for them because of their size.  I purchased this item and I can assure you this is the BEST purchase I have made so far.  It actually works exactly as shown.  My two cats took to it immediately.  Very well made, easy to handle, cuts down on odor, and the dragging out of the litter is cut down tremendously.  My cats love their new litter box, and it is not an eye sore as was the open one I had.  I think every cat owner should have this box.

Entry  1: ( March 18, 2014):Just purchased this item and our 5 months old kitten, Mexican born  Miso, and recent immigrant to New York City, took to it immediately. It was easy to assemble and to clean and it operated as described. I will keep you posted on further developments. One issue I have with this device is that it should have been made of better plastic. The plastic seems of poor quality.  So as a consequence my review should be a 4 3/4 stars, not a 5.Entry 2: March 24, 2014:Have been using the litter box now for one week. It is still extremely easy to use, although care must be exercise to add cat litter until it is at the level marked on the outside of the litter box. One complaint I have about the litter box is that it releases a small amount of litter in the course of operating it, but this is nothing serious as it is just a few grains.  This could have been remedied if the  designer of the litter box had used more clamps for  attaching the top half of the litter box to the bottom half, not only the three clamping levers it currently uses.I am lowering my review to a 4 1/2 stars due to the clamp issue, and due to the next reasons mentioned. Some people might find having to clean up the odd grains of cat litter that fall through the sides of the  top lid an issue.  I also think much sturdier plastic should have been used for the overall construction of the litter box. For seniors who might find difficult monitoring the litter box through the front aperture, the design of the top lid should have included a transparent plastic window to make it easier to look inside of the litter box.I am very pleased with this litter box. I think this litter box would be too small for a very large cat. For a single cat that is not very heavy and large it should work fine.

The disposal drawer isn't larger/wide enough for clumped urine. I ended up throwing the plastic liter filter away and just scooping the liter by hand - using it as a covered literbox.  Rolling the literbox wasn't as good in practice as it first sounded either.

I've seen the Cat Whisperer say this wouldn't work well but we've had ours for 5 years and love them! (we have 3 because we have 6 cats) You never have to scoop! I had shoulder surgery so scooping litter boxes daily was hard, with this you simply roll the unit and empty the bin (it doesn't get any easier than that). Our cats have zero issues using this. Locking tabs hold the lid on, easy to take apart to clean and fill. The secret is rolling it slowly and tapping on the bottom to get anything that's stuck due to moisture. This is a gem and I recommend it to any cat owner. Sturdy too, ours are 5 years old and counting!

Wow...I have NO idea why everyone doesn't use these!  This will sound like hyperbole, but I'm not lying when I say that emptying the litter box is almost a pleasure with the Omega Paw!  It's so amazingly easy, and it takes less than a minute to do.  We've found that rolling the box very slowly helps a ton, as it cuts down on the amount of good litter that ends up in the disposal tray.  If you go nice and slow in both direction, you'll get only clumps in there, and you'll be amazed at how easy this system is.  I can't recommend it highly enough -- just buy one already!

Awesome! specially for people who don't wanna lose a lot of time cleaning the litter box or are not comfortable doing it.But the litter surface is quite small for and adult cat. It is perfect until the cat is a teenager
holds the food, water and biscuits in well. There isnt any leakage on the floor anymore. Works well and is living upto a month of use. Great product for a good price.
very good holds smell perfectly

This is an incredibly clever  pseudo-automatic  self-cleaning litter box. We have five cats (all rescues) and have used two regular litter boxes in the past. Litter dust accumulates and it's just a mess to deal with. The litter cleaning process in this  rolling litter box  is brilliant AND it works like a charm. My husband is the one who handles the litter cleaning chore, and he's also reluctant to change. He didn't like it at first because our limited space where the boxes are located, but having used these boxes and realizing how easy it is to empty the Zagnut litter nuggets captured in the tray, he's completely on board. We use MUCH less litter -- about a third of what we used to use, because on the litter that's stuck to the nuggets winds up in the disposal tray. The rest goes back to the box. Like I said, it's geeeeeenius.Buy one for yourself, get good litter (such as Dr. Elsey's) and you'll clean up your casa and reduce the cost and headache of litter changing. You'll thank me for it later!  :-D

Easy to put together, durable, and really easy to use. My cats got a hang of using it after several days (cats tend to not like new items in their area), but I had to keep their old litter box next to it until they started using this one regularly. Makes clean up very easy (and kind of fun) - I don't know why I didn't buy this sooner.I'll probably invest in another one. My cats are bigger (probably 15+ lbs?) but they have no problem using this, it seems spacious enough inside even for my big boy. I highly recommend this product.
It takes too much space and is  not easy to clean.  I think a new design is in order for my tastes.  My cat was not particular about this box either.

This is a very bulky item when both parts are connected.  With a bad back and the weight of a litter-filled box, the rolling was not going to work for me.  I use the bottom part of the box alone  as a regular litter pan.  I suppose the top could be another litter pan; there doesn't seem to be any difference in the strength of the plastic.  Maybe this would be a good solution for someone else.

This  Omega Paw  self cleaning litter box  is NOT sturdy!  The parts that snap together do NOT fit, and  if they fit  would be very easily to break off.  and  to operate the box, you have to turn it...  and it just is NOT a good product!
I tossed my littermaid when this arrived.  I use crystal litter and it's just perfect, my cats give it the seal of approval.

I was unsure about which size to get because I have a fairly small cat. The large box was only five bucks more than the regular, so I went for it. I saw pictures of the regular box next to a cat that weighs slightly less than mine (6lbs, my cat's 7-8lbs) and it looked like a tight fit, so I spent $5 extra to ensure my cat's comfort and am coping with the fact that it's just barely too big to fit where I'd ideally like to put it, haha. Nearly an entire half of these rolling-style boxes are off limits to cats because that's where all the internal mechanics are (the litter filter, the clump-holder), so even though the smaller sizes look decent, your best bet is to go for the largest which I think will fit most kitties comfortably, even the heftier ones :PYou need to use clumping litter with this box, but that's not a big deal. When cleaning, you have to roll it quite far over, almost onto its roof, then give the bottom a couple taps and you'll hear any stuck bits of litter release and fall into the holding compartment, then lastly you turn it back in the opposite direction, nearly onto its roof again, and you'll feel the weight shift as the clean litter evenly distributes itself back into the cat-accessible portion. It's super easy.It does feel like it could be a bit sturdier, the latches are kind of flimsy, but it works. No leaks or spills thus far, the cat took to it immediately, and it saves me a lot of time and trouble. The previous box was in the bathroom in a narrow space that was generally out of sight, but you could always smell when the cat had been in there.. not with this box! It's currently in my bedroom (trust me, it'll be relocating once I find a new place for it. It's in there temporarily because it won't fit where the old one was and I haven't found a new spot yet) and I literally don't even know when she's used it! I almost forget to clean it because there's no smell at all, despite the entrance being open and door-less.If you have a cat(s), you need this. Way cheaper than other boxes of similar nature. Sure, it's not ENTIRELY self-cleaning, but it's painfully simple and I can take 20 seconds out of my day to roll a litter box over if it'll save me a few hundred bucks!
The medium is okay, but the large is a waste of money, the sliding clips don't work right, some don't line up at all and they break off in no time.
I am amazed at how great this thing is. I used a little duct tape to seal the inside  scoop area  but other than that it is by far the best litter box I've ever seen or had. Everyone is amazed by it!
Did not work as well as I thought it would. Maybe I just need some practice.

Nice, large litter box; however, the self-cleaning isn't functional with the one we received. We use the natural pine pellets, so I'm giving this a 3-star rating because it may not work due to the pellets being so large? Maybe if we switch to the sandy-like clumping pine it would work better? I'm not sure...we're going to finish using the pine pellets we currently have first & then try the clumping pine to see if it makes a difference. If so, I will update. For now, it's just a nice, big litter box that I still have to clean with pooper scooper.

Initially seemed like a good idea, but then I noticed the cats started to stink! The tabs are too flimsy to disassemble, clean it, and reassemble. Several snapped off. Clumped, dirty litter got stuck in the grate that was supposed to filter out the waste. I do think the cats liked the cave-like feel of it, but when you think about how the tumbling coats the walls with urine and feces, it's kind of gross

I threw this out after just a couple of weeks, the littler sticks to the walls and big clumps are stuck to the ceiling, I can't have that falling on my cat when she's trying to do her stuff.  Awful invention!

The rolling to clean feature of this litter box is a novel idea, but in practice it doesn't work all that well. The top of the litter box gets very dirty and requires frequent cleanings, when you roll it over some litter falls out of the cracks around the side (even though it's clipped shut) which means you have to vacuum every single time that you clean the litter box.I ended up taking the filter and the drawer out of the litter box and just using it as a standard litter box. I take the lid off and scoop it out every 2 days or so. The only problem with this is that there are a couple plastic pieces on the bottom of the litter box that stick up (used to hold the grate in place) that make it annoying to scoop through.

If you have 1,2, or even 3 cats and room to place these, they really are great. However, they are bulky and do take up a lot of space.The idea behind it does work well especially if keep up with sifting them at least every other day. Any longer than that and you will have trouble removing the handy little drawer with your treasures.Unfortunately for me, some of my cats (I have 14) will NOT use them. There are a few 'bullies' and the cats who are usually the targets do not want to feel trapped, but the ones that do get used, get used plenty.Cleaning them is a bit of a pain, but if non of the cats have diarrhea and you are able to stay on a good routine, cleaning them shouldn't be necessary very often.
We purchased this litter box when we got our first Ragdoll cat. The litter box worked great until our cat got too big to use it. I would recommend this litter box if you have a smaller cat breed.

With 6 cats, I have quite a few litter boxes - 6 to be exact - 1 short of ideal one per cat + one extra.  And, given that my cats are very picky and a couple have avoidance issues, I have tried to vary not only the types of litter boxes, but the types of litter.  Now, most of my cats seem to be adaptable and use whatever is handy and are not picky about types/litter/etc.  Unfortunately, they are not all that way.I have a Litter-Maid automatic box in the master suite for my geriatric kitty.  She uses it without fail.  And, I'm currently on maybe number 6 of these.  If you get a good one, it is great.  Unfortunately, I have had several lemons, but the good ones keep me coming back to this type.I have a ScoopFree automatic with crystals and, so far, it works just fine.  Not all of my cats will use it, though, and, of course, replacing the trays/crystals is more expensive.I have 3  regular , open style plastic litter boxes - 2 with regular scoopable litter and 1 with newspaper.  Obviously nothing to break there.Finally, I have this which also gets filled with scoopable litter.  One of the tabs that holds the lid on securely when you roll it broke yesterday, so it is no longer able to perform as designed and will likely get thrown away.  I have had issues over the years with the tabs being difficult to close and opening unexpectedly, but they did work until now.  So, I guess 4 years is pretty good!  I have also had a little problem with the screen not staying in place, but was able to fix that.  The good is I have used this box I paid $44 for 4 years with little trouble.  The bad is that when the tabs slid open, I'd end up with used litter on my floor so I learned to always check they were closed securely before rolling.  The ugly is that this box is far from  self-cleaning .  Yes, you don't scoop - you roll.  But, as others have mentioned, not only do you still have to clean the inside, but poop can get stuck to the grid and that is a nasty job.  And, it is rather difficult to put new litter in without spilling and without taking the lid off which I didn't like to do given the issues with the tabs.I am torn about whether to replace.  I see the price is now $10 less so that is good.  Overall, even though it finally broke, I feel I received my money's worth after 4 years of use.  But, I did have more cleaning issues with this than the normal plastic, cheap, regular  non self-cleaning  boxes.  On the other hand, a couple of my cats regularly used this box, so...

Love it... love it... and agree with everything, which has been said.However, I had to adjust a bit, so I am just just listing what I find noteworthy:a) not every litter worked well for me (in the past I used a pine straw litter) now I have switched to one which is more  sandy b) you should not fill in too much litter or it will  roll  into the disposal bin, when you roll the litter bixNoteworthy on the +side: this is the first litter box I have seen, which really controls dust and contains odors, that's probably got something to do with its funny shapeI have already recommended this product to all my friends, who are cat owners. 5 paws up!

I've had this for awhile now, as I wanted to test it out before I wrote a review.  Well, it really works if you follow the directions it comes with! i'm not sure how  everything that needs to go  ends up in the little drawer to the right, but it does.  All you do is pull out the drawer and dispose of the stuff in it - then turn the littler box back to the LEFT a little to redistribute the remaining cat litter.It makes cleaning the cat box an easier, less  close up  job!

Really was skeptical that this would work.  It not only works...it's wonderful.  Easy to clean by rolling it and removing droppings out of slide in tray.  Cats like its roominess and I love the easy of cleaning the litter.Great find!

i have been using for about a week now and i love it! i never smell cat box anymore and it takes me like 2minutes to clean if not maybe less i just roll and dump and add a scoop or two of litter from the opening. i also mix about half a cup of fresh step crystals with any old cheap clumping litter and the bag is pricy around 14 dollars but i have had it for 3m and i still have tons of cyrstals.

This is the last litter box I will ever buy!  I have 2 cats and they actually enjoy using the same litter box.  I tried having a couple of them and they only used one...which meant that I was scooping all the time!  With this box I can easily clean the litter multiple times a day faster then I can make coffee :)My 9 year old also now loves cleaning the litter box...YAY.

I like this better than the traditional method of scooping cat s*it. It's faster and more convenient. It doesn't do a great job of getting all the clumps, but I just change the litter more. I find it helpful to beat the bottom of the box when its upside down to loosen the clumps that stick to the bottom of the pain. About once a week I take the lid off and actually scoop it, but through the week I just tip it over. It's still a disgusting litter box, but more bearable than the traditional box.

Good idea, but just too heavy for most people.  My husband is strong enough to turn the box so the clumps go into the removable box.  Three cats (three litter boxes) and the job to take care of them is mine since I'm  stay at home  and my husband works over 8 hours a day.  So unless you're strong, I don't recommend it.  Sorry.

I've had cats since I was around 5 years old...so let's just say over 30 years. I love cats but HATE cleaning their litter boxes. I've tried all kinds of options to make it easier/cleaner/etc. Nothing has really helped until I used this thing. Now, it literally takes me less than 5 minutes to clean the litter box without a mess or stink. I am a happy cat owner and my cat is happy that her litter is clean more often.

This is the second one I bought and I still love it. It is perfect for making my life easier with 5 cats. I just put in scoopable litter and roll it twice a day. I will say you can't buy cheap litter with this. I use the blue Purina in the 40lb boxes. Make sure you get scoopable or this product does not work.
EASY!!!!!  I abhor cleaning litter, but gotta....this makes the chore SO MUCH EASIER!!!  Just make sure you have an appropriate container to dispose of the litter and you're golden!
I have 2 of these for 2 cats and it makes it much easier to clean the litter boxes.  I would recommend this to my friends.
Naw SOOOO disappointed.it dosent work as instructed.The 'clumps' dont release themselves and you end up throwing lots of viable product.Darn.It looked so promising!

We had an electric cat box for several years and when it finally burned out I just didn't feel like spending another $149 for a new one so I gave this one a try.  I first purchased the  regular  sized one and it was waaayyy too small so I returned it and purchased the larger one.  I have never been happier...much more convenient and easier the the electric one.  No oders, easy to roll and the catch box for the used matter is fantastic.  Not much bigger space wise than a standard covered cat box.  You gotta love it!

This product pretty much saved my life. I have two very large cats and it feels like they crap their body weight daily. I bought this because scooping has been so tedious, and because there is always so much sometimes it falls out of the scoop or out of the box itself. Nasty business. But thanks to this box I don't have to worry about that. Thank you so much!

My cats won't even use the other 2 litter boxes they had been using before.  They have gone over and smelled them but haven't used them since. I bought this. The only reason I gave it a 4 star is because I have found that I do have to check to make sure some clumps were not stuck to the bottom periodically.  Otherwise, it is a five.

This thing is awesome!!!!!! So easy!!!! You have to figure out the right amount of litter to put it. You waste a lot of litter if you over fill it. But omg this thing makes scooping poo soooo easy!!!!
My cat would not go inside it.  We adopted him and I guess he is used to an open top.  We took off the top and taped up the sides.  It works well that way too.

We have two senior female cats, and I had high hopes for this thing. In concept, it's a good idea. In execution, not so much. We have had ours for a year now, and have found the following:- Screen/grate gets caught and sticks, therefore litter does not filter all that well- You still have to scoop because clumped pee sticks to the bottom no matter how much you shake and bang on the outside- The grate gets clogged with stuff, which impedes filtering- You have to hold the drawer in with your hand when you flip it, or it comes out and litter leaks all overOur grate wore out after a year and started to break/come apart, and we decided not to get another of this model. We ended up having to scoop at least every week anyway, and vacuum 2-3 times a week from the spilled litter. Not to mention taking it apart and cleaning the grate all the time. So it really didn't save us any real convenience over a traditional scooping litterbox.

Rated this before.  We bought a big and small one.  Even the big one leaves barely enough room for the cat to do his business, and he sometimes ended up kicking turds out of the box or all over the wall because of the funny doorway.Does not work very easily and is a hassle.  And it's expensive.  What a waste.
This is my 4 litter box I have bought. Gave one to my daughter for her cat and 3 are mine for my 5 cats. Great product so easy to use. Thank You

I clean out my litter boxes so much quicker.  Now that I'm pregnant I only have to wear gloves when I pull out the collection bin.  They still need cleaned every so often like my old ones (we clean them completely every 3 to 4 months with Odoban or a little bleach in a lot of water).  You also have to get used to putting them back together correctly.  Which is the whole key to having these things.  If you don't do it right then you have the problems other people have spoken about.  Don't forget once you turn it to pat the bottom of it to loosen the bottom clay litter.  I have two males and a female and the males go less often but far more urine so it's good to tap it and get that off and turned into the pale to dump.  The large box is best for larger cats.  It would never work with the smaller size in my house except for the small female I have.  You get used to taking it apart and putting it back together and now I do it just as quickly as the regular big one we have in the laundry room.  It's cleaner and quicker all the way around for cleaning out litter boxes.  Especially if you have a particular cat that wants it kept clean on a regular basis or they will Poop outside the box.  I can get all three cleaned in less than 5 minutes :)

If you find that your cats like to tinkle in the corners there is a simple solution. When you have the box upside down just falcon punch the bottom. All of the tinkle clumps will break off and fall down, ready to be removed. This thing has cut down my litter cleaning to a matter of seconds and I love it.Plus the punch method of removal means that the pee comes off the wall cleanly instead of being smeared by a scoop.

I didn't even dare put this together, seeing how thin the plastic is and how delicate its lock tabs. I have a kitty rescue ranch and hoped this would be of use.  I would order several more but it is useless to me. Just my opinion. I sent it back. Happy it works for a few, from reviews I read. Plus, you roll it over to its side, all the way over, and the clumps spill into a drawer that you empty. Sounds good? They leave out the fact it still leaves clumps stuck to the bottom that won't loosen w/o help.  Therefore the cat has to use a dirty litter box unless it is emptied after every single use. I've read reviews on this of people saying they don't have to (totally) empty but once weekly.  I feel sorry for any cat who must use dirty litter.  It was mentioned also that you might duct tape it together when the tabs break.  Wouldn't that cause a nasty build up along its edges (inside the tape) where it fits together?

Initially, I thought this was a good idea.  The cat gets his privacy, and I have a way to make an unpleasant chore a little easier.  But then I saw Galaxy Jackson on My Cat From Hell.  A couple needed help with their cat not using the litter box.  They had this litter box.  Galaxy pointed out that a cat doesn't want to be surrounded by his own urine and feces smell.  That made perfect sense.  I mean, when you think about it, you don't scrub the litter box clean, so that means some remnants, even if it's mainly smells, are left on the litter box after you clean it.  When looked at it that way, it seems pretty gross.

I got rid of the litter maid that my cat hated and pretty much attacked every time it came on.  This product works a lot better.  Sometimes automation IS NOT the better way to go. I just roll this over every morning and the litter dumps into the trough, I dispose and kitty is happy.

whoever invented this is a GENIUS!  yes, it tends to leak a wee bit of litter from the cup during rolling it back.  but that bit of dry sand is WAY less than what the cats track on the litter mat as they go in and out of the box.  the ease of keeping the litter clean 2-3x per day FAR out weighs the measly pinch of sand dribble.  bottom line:  best cat accouterment ever!

I really liked this litter box when I first bought it. I liked that it had a lid and was relatively easy to clean and use; however, after less than a year of use, I'm looking for something else. The litter started to leak out of various crevices each time I cleaned it. The plastic has warped over time leaving lots of gaps around the lid for litter to seep through. The internal grate that is supposed to filter the litter is too wide and dislodges easily from its tiny clips leaving much waste behind, which in turn leads to bad odors. I also don't like that it doesn't have a swinging door. One, the door would reduce some of the bad odors, second, the entrance is very low, so my cat spreads litter out of the box when she is digging to cover her business. Great idea, poor execution. On to the next option.

I was looking at the auto-cleaning litter boxes and came across this.  The motorized ones get a lot of bad reviews, so I was really interested in this design being manual but yet clean.  Just roll it over slowly, roll it back, tip it the other way a bit so the litter comes back into the tray and you're ready to empty the scoop.  It works great!  I was concerned about pieces getting stuck, but I haven't seen that happen yet.  You do need a little more floor space so you have room to roll it, but you could slide it and roll it if you don't have much space available.I made the mistake of over-filling it at first (used a full 40 pound bag), and that caused me to waste some litter since it all didn't fit in the sifting area and the extra went into the scoop.  Whoops. No big deal, lesson learned.

I don't mind cleaning the litter box, because now it's not a chore. It's very easy to use! I have a small apartment, so the liter box has to stay in my living room. In conjunction with the right litter and the Litter Genie, I hardly ever smell the box!The only complaint I have is that when rolling the box to clean it, the litter can get stuck in the lip of the two halves and spill out. It doesn't make a large mess, but it's enough that it requires a bit of vacuuming every so often.I also feel that an attachable door would be a nice improvement. Especially a door that can be locked close for when you are rolling the box for cleaning.I highly recommend this product!

I was just about at my wits end with the scooping and the odor and the mess. I used to like to play in the sand when I was a kid, but let's face it. This ain't sand. And this is not gold we are digging for. I tried to find one of those self-cleaning litter boxes but the problem I faced with those, besides the cost, is that they need to be plugged in and my bathroom plug is part of the light fixture over the sink. I can't have an extension cord dangling all over the place, especially in the bathroom where it could get wet. Luckily I came across this amazing life changing invention. Went together in a snap and as soon as I knew it had been visited I tried it out. Perfect. Everything did what it was supposed to do and everything went where it was supposed to go. The litter box was clean in less than a minute with no scooping and no mess. I showed it to my sister and now she's all over it too. Before you buy it, go look at a few Youtube vids. There are a ton of them and not one owner is disappointed with the functionality of this litter box.  Be aware that it is large. I got the regular size and it is big! I can't even imagine how big the larger one must be.  I guess if you have a giant Maine Coon with a weight problem you might need the larger one.  My three adult cats all fit in the regular size with no problem and my boy is a fairly large guy. I don't think you should own a cat without this box.

Great for any cat owner. It's ao easy. You just roll it over, let the poops go to the side, roll it back, and pull out the poop tray and dump. So easy, so clean, so nice

If you use this litter box the way it is advertised (rolling it over, etc.) it will accumulate poop and pee all over the roof and nasty stuff will get stuck in the  filter  portion. This litter box is one of the easiest ever to clean.It's like a poo machine - you put in some clumping litter, add a cat or two or three (one at a time is best), roll the box to the right, on to the lid and back and Ta-Da! when you pull out the neat tray on the right - you've got clumps! Nothing special... Just using a regular mans comb works better....Also, my cat got dandruff from this.... Harsh metal, kinda pointy.Completely not worth the money, do yourself a favor and buy a regular cheap plastic comb.
Where I live in Mexico, in the dry season there are some grass-weeds that get attached to the fur of my cats, and it is difficult to take it off, but this comb makes it easier.
This comb does not work on DSH cats. The teeth are too far apart to be effective our flea comb works better

I have used this product on my two twelve year-old cats who do not like being fussed with. It works very well and I am very pleased with the results. Good job! I would recommend it to any pet owner who wants to help keep their pet groomed and clean.

My cat has medium length hair that is very fine and very soft. It is hard to get it off of things once it's one there. So, I brush her regularly, particularly during the shedding season. She seems to like this brush quite a lot. It gets a lot of hair in just a few passes. I have another brush that I also like a lot (for a different reason), but that one requires a lot of passes to get the job done. The downside to this one (which is the reason I have the other one also) is that it doesn't really get hair off of items. But, it isn't advertised as such, so I am still giving it 5 stars. It does what it says it is going to do - brushes the cat well.

I'm figuring the best way to help you decide if this might be good for your dog is to tell you the basics about mine's play habits. She'll grab her plush toys (stuffed animals w/ squeakers) occasionally and I can throw them maybe 4-5 times before her doggy brain decides she has an even better idea and brings me the rubber Chuck It. So I try to encourage her to grab her plush 'babies' in the house, but she's a dog so... I needed an indoor ball.I then tried the  indoor Chuck It . That toy is larger, like this one, and although it's also plush on the outside, it is much firmer than this one. She didn't like it. She never picks it, and will only play with it for a very short time if I try to replace the tennis ball she brings me with the indoor, plush, Chuck It. She seems not to like that it's bigger and harder to just grab up in her mouth so then she's right back to dropping the rubber ball in my lap and play has to end (again, because she's a dog and so can't understand why we can't just throw the ball she wants instead). I needed a new indoor ball.I was skeptical about this ball and it took me a while to commit. Since it says it's 8  I knew it'd be about the same size as the indoor Chuck It and I believed the biggest reason she didn't like that toy was because it was pretty large to get her whole mouth around - even for a bigger dog. I finally pulled the trigger because there's just no such thing as a normal-sized plush tennis ball (because that would just be a regular tennis ball lol) and I needed something. Well... she got it for Christmas and she hasn't stopped playing with it since (it's Feb. 6th today - and we just finished playing with again when I decided to sit down and write this). She grabs it immediately and every day. The big difference between this ball and the indoor Chuck It is that this ball is a traditional plush, meaning it's squishy as well as plush, and I think that's what makes the difference for my dog. She can 'squish' it down into the ground as she's cramming it all into her mouth and that makes it easy to pick up and carry. Half the time she brings it to me but then won't actually let anyone have it! lol She loves it. And I'm so happy to finally have an indoor ball  that I don't have to worry about hitting something and breaking it. I certainly don't want things to hit the TV, period, but if this ball did, it would have the same impact as a stuffed animal hitting the screen so no worries - unlike a tennis ball or even the  indoor  Chuck It.It has a squeaker, which my dog loves in all her toys. She specifically seeks out the 'squeak' whenever she picks up any toy and will bite several areas of a given toy to find the squeak. However, I will say this squeaker could probably be just a bit larger to accommodate the larger toy size because the dog does have a slightly tougher time finding the squeaker and many times doesn't find it at all (it still doesn't discourage her from wanting to play with it though, and that's saying something in itself because usually if she can't 'find the squeak' on a toy she doesn't want anything to do with it for very long).As this is a traditional plush, I wouldn't recommend it for heavy chewers/shredders as it won't hold up any better than any other stuffed dog toy. My dog isn't hard on her toys even though she plays with them often, so her only holey toys are those that have worn with age. Since she's had some since before she was one and is now eight I think it's safe to say she's not a toy destroyer at all. :) You can tell this ball is well stitched though, and I believe will last probably the rest of my dog's life as it seems well made of quality material (doesn't feel thin/cheap and seams are all solidly closed/tight). With the Easy Harness he did get better in not pulling as much but would still pull at times. But, it did nothing to curb his lunging at dogs and bikes. It was getting frustrating walking him as he would bark at no apparent reason. If you know how to use it, this collar can be helpful in training your dog to not pull as much. But, don't expect miracles, you still need to do your part to train your dog.Fast forward 3 months to the head halter. I heard about gentle leader but was apprehensive in getting it. In putting on the gentle leader my dog did fuss and not want it on him. He would try to take it off by pawing at it and rubbing his face on bushes. It has been 5 days and still does it but he is getting used to it. Reward him with treats after so he associates as positive. So does it work? YES! But, be sure you know how to use it. Watch the DVD! it is important you don't send your dog mixed signals by keeping it tense. On our first walk the dog did pull and lunge but he did not like the feeling, especially when lunging. But on our first walk I could tell he was staying by my side much better. I did not expect it to prevent lunging but it has. I think it makes him think twice. I have taken him past houses where dogs will bark it him, in the past he would try to go to the barking but now he just whimpers and keeps walking. This produce truly is working wonders (the gentle leader).So in short, I would recommend both the Easy Walk and Gentle Leader. If you have a problem it does not hurt to try both and see which one works better for your dog. But keep in mind you have to do your part to still train your dog. These products are meant as tools. For my purpose, Gentle Leader has done wonders.The only complaint i have on gentle leader is i wish there was padding on the part that goes over the snout. After taking it off you can see the impression it makes on his snout when removed. But not sure if padding would render this product less effective or not. But, no I do not consider this product as abusive or cruel. It is a tool to help him understand what is expected of him on walks.

We've got two large rescue dogs (60 and 85 lbs., respectively) and, though they did have puppy class, because there were two of them--not that we planned to keep either; we're failed fosters--they didn't get the sort of individual obedience attention our previous pooch did. To the point we almost never did it, just because it was so unpleasant both for us, and them. (Choking themselves the whole way and practically pulling us off our feet at least one or two times per walk.) We either had to have two adults do the walk, one for each dog, where they would then constantly compete with each other to see who could be in front. Or, we had to take them one at a time, with the one at home going absolutely bonkers about being left behind. It was, shall we say, less than ideal.Then I saw the Gentle Leader and thought, 'Well, it's worth a shot.' Not expecting much I ordered one, to test it out. Fitted on our larger, yet slightly less truculant dog and saw an immediate difference. Walked him around the neighborhood with a loose leash, for the first time ever, and only minor objections--pawing at it once or twice--to the nose strap. I immediately ordered a second head collar for other dog and we've been walking them together every day since.Neither loves the strap, but, honestly, it seems extremely gentle compared to the constant self-choking they did when the leash was attached to their regular collars and we were constantly battling to hold them. The brochure compares it to reins on a horse (without the bit, obviously), which makes sense to me. Today, for the first time in the two year we've had them, I took both for a walk at the same time, successfully and with very little pulling, even when we ran into a neighbor's dog loose in their yard. In the past, all three would have ended up running around loose, with me probably on the ground, but this time I was able to hold them fairly easily and with absolutely no drama.Hopefully we'll someday be able to go back to the standard collar, without the pulling, but, for now, my husband and I call it the  Miracle Leash  and I'm 100 percent sold!

My cat (a very large Maine Coone) had a cute collar that I thought was a breakaway collar when I bought it.  Then a few weeks ago, part of his tag go caught on a blanket he was lying on and he began to struggle, actually choking himself more in the process.  By the Grace of God, I just happened to be sitting across the room when it happened.  I couldn't untangle the collar, so I quickly pulled it over his head (luckily it was very loose; I always keep my cat's collar loose for emergencies).  If it hadn't been loose, he would have died.My poor cat!  I felt horrible that he had to go through such a traumatic event!  I immediately went online and found this breakaway collar.  When it arrived, I tested it by pulling it apart with my hands and it came apart immediately.  I feel partially guilty because when I made the decision to buy his initial collar, it was a cute sports collar with the logo of a team that we admire.  That was more uppermost in my mind than my cat's potential safety!  How cute he would look sporting that collar.Now I have peace of mind!  We were very lucky and I thank God that my cat didn't choke to death on his collar.  I will NEVER EVER buy him a collar that isn't a break-away collar again.  Also, p.s., I don't put any cute jewelry or little things that can get caught on his collar anymore.  All he has on his collar is his tag, and I am still very superstitious so I keep his collar very loose.I have read the truly heart-rending stories of what has happened to other people's pets on this website.  My heart goes out to them.  I have lost pets in the past, and I know how terrible that pain is.  I feel for every person who is suffering.  The only comfort is in knowing that animals all go to heaven where they are well-cared for and will never suffer again.For people who do not have breakaway collars on their pets, you are gambling with your pet's life.  It only takes mere minutes for your animal to die!  And the more the animal is caught, the harder he/she will struggle and the more he/she will choke.  I can tell you that from experience.  My cat panicked trying to break free and it just made it worse.More education should be done about the importance of using break-away collars for pets.  Non-breakaway collars should be outlawed, in my humble opinion.

I have five rescued dogs, all of whom have a varying affinity for toys. Peedee, for example, enjoys things that go squeak; when she’s feeling especially saucy, Mags delights in ripping fluffy faux animals apart; and Rennie loves all the things, from chasing tennis balls to chewing on rubber Kongs. I figured that, between the five of them, someone would get a kick out of the Kyjen Hide-A-Squirrel Puzzle Toy. As it turns out, it was a near-universal hit.Though my dogs are all on the small side (twelve to twenty-five pounds), I sprang for the Ginormous size for the maximum amount of hiding space. It has four front-facing holes, as well as one large hole on top. Each hole measures about 2  to 3 inches across, which is wide enough to fit a standard size tennis ball. The included squirrels (this unit comes with six) also fit through quite easily (but not so easily that they don’t sometimes prove a challenge). At 13  inches high, it’s a little shorter than my smallest dog - but the holes sit all different heights.The squirrels are pretty standard as far as plush toys go – by which I mean they’re easily torn apart. If your dog is a rough chewer, and you want to make the squirrels last as long as possible, supervised play is highly recommended. Luckily, Peedee and Rennie so enjoy retrieving the squirrels from their tree trunk that they don’t mind (too much!) when I take the toys away to re-hide them. That said, if your dog does manage to plow through all the squirrels, you can also buy replacements separately – or use the tree trunk to hide other toys. Rennie tends to fixate on tennis balls, and the holes are a perfect fit!So far my dogs haven’t shown any interest in chewing the tree trunk, but I suppose that’s something to watch out for. After all, it’s soft and plush and thus ripe for the picking. It looks well-made, but the materials obviously aren’t tough enough to withstand the jaws of a determined dog.Incidentally, I’ve also purchased a number of puzzle toys for my dogs; our smartest guy, Peedee, is the only one who shows much interest in the more challenging ones. This one definitely falls on the easy end of the spectrum, making it an excellent choice for the not-so-bright dogs in your pack (*cough* Rennie *cough*).  If you can use your dog’s favorite toys to provide extra motivation, all the better.4.5 stars, rounded up to 5 on Amazon. This would be a five-star deal if the trunk or squirrels were made of sturdier materials.

The video review that customer  ~*Just Me *~  posted on 3/23/2010 was also helpful, even though she doesn't tell us what size Twist 'n Treat she bought.DOES MY DOG LIKE IT?Yes, my dog likes the Twist 'n Treat.  Why?  Because it dispenses treats so easily!WHAT I DIDN'T KNOW...The Twist 'n Treat has openings on both sides. The openings are the same size, and they are directly opposite each other. So, treats fall-out quickly.But don't they say you can screw down the Twist 'n Treat to lessen the number of treats it dispenses?  Yes, you can; however... The 2 openings on each side are semi-circles (one set of semi-circles on the bottom of the Twist 'n Treat, and another set of semi-circles on the top of the Twist 'n Treat). When closing the Twist 'n Treat, you screw the top part into the bottom part. Then...#1If the semi-circles on each side do not line-up to form a circle, then no treats will be dispensed (unless I unscrew it a lot, and then treats fall-out very easily all around the Twist 'n Treat, because the gap all around the Twist 'n Treat is too large).#2If I screw the Twist 'n Treat all the way down and line-up the semi-circles, then the treats will not dispense, because the opening is not large enough.#3If I unscrew the Twist 'n Treat half a turn with the semi-circles still lined-up, then the treats will dispense; however, now they fall-out too easily/quickly from the 2 openings (my dog was able to get all the treats out in about 1 minute). At this point, I tried to screw the Twist 'n Treat just a little bit to the right in order to lessen the opening size (so the semi-circles were not lined-up exactly), but I couldn't  get it just right . And I really don't want to have to  get it just right  every time I use the Twist 'n Treat...this toy shouldn't be difficult for me to use!!!#4What if I offset the 2 sets of semi-circles so that a treat barely fits through the openings? Nope. If I do that, then I have 4 semi-circles/openings, and the treats dispense even quicker.OTHER NOTESIt is made in China, but it appears to be well made.The small size is 3 inches in diameter.It sits 2.25 inches tall when screwed all the way down.The outer shell is about 3/16 inch thick.The female opening is about 1/8 inch thick (where you screw the top into the bottom).The plastic is not hard, but not soft; it feels rubbery.It's easy to clean.It smells like rubber, but your nose has to be close to smell it.It is quiet on hardwood floors.When screwing it down, there is enough resistance to keep the opening by itself. The maximum opening size is about 5/8 inch (any larger opening and the item will open by itself when your dog plays with it). When screwed all the way down, the opening size is about 1/4 inch.It holds only about 2 tablespoons of treats. If I tried to put more treats in it, then they either fall-out while I'm trying to load it; or I have to close it, block one of the openings, and load treats into the other opening one at a time (not fun).  If you overfill it and then screw it down, then the treats get compacted on the inside, and they will not fall-out.Here is what is on the packaging that came with it: Small for dogs 8-20 pounds (Yorkie, Jack Russell, Pug). Dishwasher safe, top rack only. Chew strength (a diagram of a bone with  soft  on the left,  hard  on the right, with a marker near the soft side). CAUTION: Not recommended for strong chewers.
