They had previously been treated with Fizzion, which seemed to do the trick, but with the warmer weather and increased humidity, the smell returned.  When I went to a website that my veterinary clinic linked to, I saw they were selling Thornell Animal Odor Eliminator.  Having never heard of this company, I did some online research, read some good reviews, and decided to give it a try.  Frankly, almost all such products have praises as well as disappointed customers, so I guess it depends on your situation and sense of smell.  Thornell smells to me like a man's cologne. The ongoing negative is one of the legs falls off regularly, startling the cat using the bed (and the bed sags a little without the leg support). It is either molded wrong or needs a better retaining mechanism. At some point I'll probably just superglue the leg onto the bed...The  Thermo  part is a small heating element, similar to a miniature (human) heating pad. It sits between two layers of foam, under the outer cover. At 6W, it adds a gentle warmth to the bed without using much power or overheating the cat. Combined with kitty's own body heat, it works well indoors. It would likely be ineffective in an unheated space. The heating element is likely part of the plastic smell.The  heated  is a nice touch that the cats seem to appreciate. I use a small (human) heating pad under another cat-bed for a similar effect, but that would be difficult to do with a window seat, and uses more power.Despite the mixed reviews, this is definitely a good window bed. It can be a little iffy to install, it could be a little softer, it could smell better, and it could be a little cheaper. I've had two of these crates for about 7-8 months now for my boxer puppies. If my story doesn't highlight how cheaply constructed these things are and how horrible of a product it is than I'm not sure what will-About an hour after putting my pups to bed, I was awaken by a sound that can only be described as a nightmare sound for any pet owner- a LOUDLY yelping puppy in her crate. I immediately rushed to see what the issue was. At first glance she seemed fine, she was just sitting there with a sad look on her face, so I went to pet her and she yelped out in pain, loudly and repeatedly, over and over; squirming because she didn't know what was wrong. Neither did I... until I saw that HER FOOT WAS IMPALED BY ONE OF THE CHEAPLY CONSTRUCTED VERTICAL METAL BARS. Apparently my 25lb 5 month old boxer was somehow able to kick one of the side bars and it came almost completely off the side where it was supposed to be soldered on. The only part that held was the top of the car, while the bottom of the bar stuck out freely and as a result she was able to get her paw through the opening that was created and the, I assume, when she retracted her foot the bottom of the bar impaled the area between the toes. When I say  impaled  I mean it, the bar went through through her soft tissue. I ended up cutting the bar off with wire cutters and removing the piece of metal from my pup's foot. It was an absolute nightmare and afterwards I immediately went out the next day and bought them both different kennels.Some points to consider about my story-A) I read and followed all guidelines and they had been using the crates for months without issue (although apparently after 5 months of age puppies are strong enough to kick out the bars).B)The divider partition was in use and they had enough space according to the instructions- which is that the space they have must be enough for them to stand up fully and turn around fully, so that was NOT the problem.C) She was just a 5 month puppy, who was already sleeping prior to me putting her in bed. Also, they were in the room right next to me, and my walls are paper-thin, so I know she wasn't writhing around inside the cage and trying to get out or anything. More likely I would guess that she went to adjust herself and the bar got bent back easily when she hit it with her leg, and when she retracted it back in that's when it became impaled (the bar had a bit of a  point  on the bottom). This is the only explanation I have as the bar was intact and not bent when I put her to bed. This means that the bars themselves are soldered on in a rather disgustingly cheap fashion. I confirmed this myself by pulling on some other bars vertical around the crates- they are indeed constructed like absolute crap and you can pull many of the points where they are soldered on right off easily.I bought these crates, TWO of them, due to good reviews, so perhaps the manufacturer started becoming lazy and/or changed their QA process. Either way, I wouldn't suggest purchasing these crates unless you're willing to live with the possibility that your 25lb dog is going to impale themselves on accident. I certainty won't be purchasing a single thing from this company again, and will have to think of a use for these $75 dangerous paper weights.

I have been very happy with this fountain overall.  I really only have one con so I'll start there, the adjustable flow is not that much different between low and high. On my pros I will note some things where I have read complaints from people on this fountain regarding this that were just common sense to expect and therefore not cons.I've had the PetMate fountain in the past and only one of my cats would use it as it was very loud, that is very much an improvement with the Drinkwell, if kept full and the motor maintained it is very quiet, my fish tank motors are louder.  But for those who expect completely silent I add by quiet, yes you can hear water running, but that should be expected when you order this trickle style design verses a flow design.  Any motorized fountain will make some noise, what impresses me is that the motor is very silent.For a fountain the maintenance is rather easy.  Yes it's weekly but if wanted main range free pet care we'd have pet rocks.  Most the parts are top rack dishwasher safe and a soft pipe cleaner style brush us all you need for nooks and crannies and the motor.  Rubbing under some hot running water weekly will clear any saliva/hair/slime off the motor parts and for and build ups a little vinegar solution does the trick.  Just be sure to rinse it clear.  The motor is tricky to take apart but my husband has no trouble doing it even though I always struggle.The filters are not that expensive as far as filters go and unit will still function without a filter for people who do not wish to use or cannot afford the carbon.  If your using already filtered water all it really serves is to stop large debris from getting to motor and removing any airborne particular that may contaminate the water.  I haven't looked into it but it may be possible to cut a thin foam filter from fish tank floss if you want to avoid carbon.  You will get some carbon dust in bowl no matter how well you rinse filter, it annoys me but it's also pretty common with carbon.I top it off once or twice a day and empty, clean, and refill weekly. If your looking for something you don't have to bother with and your reason for buying a fountain is that filling regular water bowls is too time consuming for you, consider a unit with a reservoir and just pay the extra money.  For us that's a non issue as we have time, we bought a fountain to increase pet fresh water intake not ease if use.  But for others maybe not so much free time.  Better pay more from the start then have to buy a different model later and pay twice.  In all honesty the least maintenance is a normal ceramic/glass bowl replaced twice daily.  Fountains, gravity waterers, drip bottles all are harder to clean and take more work overall.Animal preference to unit has been mixed to positive.  One of our three cats (a confident alpha) took to this immediately and I have noted an increase in his drinking.  My eldest still goes to the gravity bowls but will also drink out if this if she is by it without hesitation, she wouldn't go near the PetMate.  Our middle child is a middle child and snubs it one to spite us (yeah really she's an I'm only going to do it if it was my idea type cat) and two because she still prefers the fine stream we can create in the sink.  We gave it an honest 2 week go by placing her by the water fountain every time she asked for sink water but alas no luck.  As she is UTI prone we finally caved and she's back to the sink.  Maybe in her own time she will choose to use it, on the plus as much of a fraidy cat as she is, the sound didn't bother her, just the stream was not as thin as she likes.  She tried to use it a few times but always backed off after one or two licks.

Did a 25 day test w/ World's Best Cat Litter Clumping Litter Formula, Nature's Miracle Just for Cats Corn Cob Litter, and Just the Crystals Premium Crystal Cat Litter.  I've also previously used Dr. Elsy's Precious Cat Ultra Premium Cat Litter and can offer a comparison with it as well.(#1) World's Best:  Clumps very well and doesn't track much at all.  There is a small amount of dust, but the dust appears to have a large particle size and doesn't stay airborne, so it settles quickly back into the box instead of getting all over everything.  There is a slight odor to the litter which is a little unusual, but it doesn't smell bad, and it seems to control the cat odor well.  It's also light weight, which makes it easy to scoop.  My four cats had no problem w/ World's Best.  Of the four litters, this is the one I'll probably end up going back to.  Some people look at the cost per pound and say it is too expensive, but it is less dense than the clay litters, and as a result it takes less poundage to fill a litter box.  While I didn't measure this precisely, I'd tend to say the 28 lbs bag of World's Best goes at least as far as a 40 lbs bag of Precious Cat (or other fine clay litter), which makes the costs a lot more comparable (just don't overpay for the litter - some of the Amazon marketplace resellers gouge on the price).(#2 - tie) Just the Crystals: I tried this litter based on the excellent reviews here on Amazon.  It doesn't track very much at all (and given the large granules, it is easy to vacuum up when it does).  It is easier to scoop than the others, as you just scoop out the poop and then stir it - you don't need to remove the urine.  While that sounds a bit gross, it really doesn't appear to get wet, smelly, or dirty any quicker than the others.  I was also really impressed with the manufacturer, who definitely seems to stand behind their brand.  All of that said, while Just the Crystals is much less dusty than the clay litters, it did create a small amount of airborne dust while scooping.  It wasn't particularly objectionable, but was more than either Nature's Miracle (which had none) or World's Best (which settled before getting very airborne).  My cats also used this box less than the others, though they've never used a crystal litter before and likely just aren't used to it, which I can't hold against Just the Crystals.  The verdict?  I probably won't continue with Just the Crystals myself, but if I used an automatic litter box this would probably be my litter of choice.  Price does seem a little bit more than other premium litters when measured by volume (not weight), but because you don't throw out the peed up litter, you still have just as much litter in the box after 3 weeks as you had when you filled it initially (versus the other litters where you're steadily throwing away litter as it gets peed up), which balances things out a bit.(#2 - tie) Nature's Miracle: Basically zero dust, very lightweight (so it is really easy to scoop), and it also smells great coming out of the package.  It does track a bit more than the others, though that's only a minor annoyance to me (could be worse depending on where the box is).  The real problem though is that it doesn't clump well, and since the clumps fall apart, small pieces of old, peed up litter gradually build up in the box, which means it starts smelling bad faster.  While I used Nature's Miracle for years, this is eventually what pushed me away from it.  If they could fix the clumping issue, this would probably be my favorite litter because of the non-existent dust and light weight.  The clumping issue is a fairly big deal to me though, and World's Best gets me most of the advantages without that major disadvantage.  Per unit of volume this seems comparable to other premium litters - perhaps a bit less than World's Best or Just the Crystals - but you might need to change it more often to keep it from smelling bad, which could make it less cost effective.(#3) Dr. Elsy's Precious Cat: Clumps extremely well and controls odor quite well.  When I had a stray cat and her kittens, this is the litter I picked once they were of age to use a litter box (rather, I used the kitten version of it) because it seemed to control the odor the best for the longest period of time.  It does track a bit more than the litters with larger granules (like World's Best or Just the Crystals), and it's fairly heavy, which makes it harder to scoop and change.  The worst part is the dust though.  As the litter ages, the granules seem to break down into smaller pieces that go airborne and make absolutely awful dust.  The older it got, the worse it became.  Scooping it would set off the smoke alarm in the room, and I had to wipe down everything in the room with a wet rag to remove the thick coating of litter dust.  With one box in the past (prior to this test), it eventually got bad enough I felt like I had to cover my mouth while scooping it.  I've tried their Respiratory Relief version as well, and that wasn't any better.  I've also tried mixing it with a less dusty litter like Nature's Miracle, but that made little difference.  Price per unit volume seems a bit less than World's Best or Just the Crystal's (more comparable to Nature's Miracle - maybe a little less than it too), but I wouldn't use it anymore even if it were free - can't stand the dust.As for test methodology...  All of the boxes were changed the same day.  They were also washed before changing them using fragrance free detergent (I use fragrance free laundry detergent to do the boxes - it's mild, leaves no odor, and I'm sure won't irritate my cats).  The litter boxes are converted from large Rubbermaid totes (I needed something with high sides as I have one cat that sometimes doesn't squat and pees over the sides of regular litter boxes).  I scoop them once daily at night.While all of the boxes are pretty large (again, they're Rubbermaid storage totes), one is about 50% larger than the others.  Historically, my cats have preferred that box, perhaps because of the extra room.  In this test, that box had World's Best, and, true to form, they used that box more than the others.  That said, the box size may factor into that.Also, I did not actually measure volume for the price comparisons.  Those are very loose estimates based on how much it felt like I needed to dump into the boxes to fill them.  At the end of the day, the price differences between them weren't so significant as to be the major differentiator between them.

There are some great things about this scratching post, and a couple things that might not be obvious that some people will want to know.Some of the  pros  will also be  cons  for some of you.WHAT I LIKE ABOUT IT:- VERY tall! Almost twice as tall as most others I've seen & bought. My cats are BIG and this is the first post that lets them fully stretch.- As scratch posts go, this is well made. The materials feel stronger than most others I've purchased and the sisal is MUCH more tightly knit together than the standard  rope in a circle  posts. This unit looks and feels like it is tightly carpeted rather than wound.- Easy assembly. Although it still arrives in a few pieces and requires assembly with a couple of screws (like most do) it is very easy to put together. All you need is a screw driver and about 2 minutes, done.- Appearance (the good part). This looks much nicer in a living room than the common circular / rope post. It looks more like a piece of furniture meant for a living room.WHAT I DON'T LIKE AS MUCH ABOUT IT (and this is being really picky):- The wood used doesn't look like real wood (as it did in some of the photos when I purchased it). It is clearly particle-board with some varnish coating.- Appearance (the not so good part) - The pictures in the description (at the time I bought it) did not clearly show the VERY obvious seam down the middle of two sides and ALSO through the base. The base is two separate pieces of wood, and after assembly the seams are very visible and very pronounced. Also; there are two VERY visible screws / holes on the top piece of wood. These facts take a bit away from the otherwise really nice appearance. At first I was very disappointed about the seams and the screw-holes at the top being so visible, but I kind of got over it fairly quickly.- The sisal fiber is very slick - as if coated, with kind of a  plastic  sort of feel to it, rather than the usual raw non-coated sisal rope feel of a common cat scratch post.- The sisal fiber coating is so tight against it that at first it seems it's not obvious to some cats that it's meant for the same thing. They have a harder time digging their claws into it than plain sisal rope.UP FOR DEBATE / WILL VARY:- It's easy to tell that some cats will not take to this like a common scratch post. My cats were unsure of it at first when I replaced it into their old common post spot. For the first 5 days I was really worried that they weren't going to use it, but after that they started to (phew!).  We have now had this for about 28 days, and during the past 16 days they've started to use it more.- For some folks the large size of this might not be suitable. It caught me a bit off-guard, but fortunately we had a good spot for it. For some of you it might not be practical due to the sheer size. It takes up considerably more space than most common posts.- Don't throw your old post away just yet. I'd recommend putting your old one in a different room so your cats still have that to go to if they don't like the unusual coating and pattern of the sisal (and in case they don't like the slick wood base as opposed to carpeted ones).- You could possibly hide the screws in the top by placing some kind of decoration on it (maybe a vase) but then you take the chance of your cats getting bonked over the head with whatever you set on the top, as the surface is slick / varnished particle board.- I think the coated sisal fiber and it's pattern make it harder for cats to get their claws in and do what they would naturally do with the common sisal rope types. (My cats, however, are adapting).SUMMARY:This is clearly a higher quality post than most and it's obvious why it is a bit pricey. It is really nice! On the other hand, I think a bit more could have been done to hide the seams and that the screws in the top. As long as you realize that the seams are very visible, and that it is much larger than  normal , and that you're taking a gamble on whether or not your cats will like it, I'd say give it a try. It's definitely nice, but maybe not exactly what some folks might be expecting in terms of appearance and materials. Ultimately my cats get to decide; and they have decided they'll use it and we were  allowed  to replace the old fashioned post with this. But we still have the old one in another room, and they still go to that instead sometimes. Overall I'm happy with the purchase.* I've taken some detailed photos to post if Amazon will let me add them to Customer Photos on this listing. If not, then I'd say there are some things about it that someone doesn't want you to see before you buy it ;-)

My little girl loved being able to see out and finally got over her fear of being in the car. She a tea cup model so helped a lot.  If riding with spouse I just put it on my lap and used a seatbelt attachment to her lead ring. Made of solid foam. Cover can be washed but hard to get back on.
Our car travels just got safer. I use it for my 7 lb yorkie; it makes sure that she is safe and can see out of windows when I'm driving. The design is very simply and materials are ok.

I have purchased three of these. Two for my dogs and one for my brother's dog. The dogs just love it. Their own place to sit and sleep. High enough to see out and they are secure! Easy to remove the cover and washes nicely. (We had a bit of car sickness.) There is also a long narrow one that will fit on a console in some vehicles, we like this one best.

Our mini dachshund loves this!  It works well in the car, but most of the time sits on the floor next to my desk.  The medium is a bit large for her at her 10# size.  She doesn't mind at all.  Very nice quality.

My little guy weighs 17#, 6 months old, long bodied and leggy, a mixed breed.  The issue that I was more concerned about was whether the car AC would be able to give him adequate cool air circulation.  I live south of Tampa, Florida and it gets mighty hot in the car during most of the year.  With the high sides, thickness and fleece like lining I was afraid he would be too hot.  This design works fine.  The seat height is just tall enough with the little front dip of the seat that I can aim the passenger vents right at him, even with him lying down, I can see his fur blowing.  And he does love to suck up the AC.  He seems to like the seat, stays in it, thinks he's all that since he can now look out the windows without standing on me while driving.  I have just enough give in the restraining leash that with the window rolled down he can just get his head out the window with his front legs on the foam edge of the bed. Seat seems secure once buckled in the passenger seat, he has plenty of space for more growing room and still be able to curl up and nap.  Knowing that he is secured in his seat and not bothering me makes for safer driving habits, for sure.  I have a 2011 Hyundai Sonata and this medium bed takes up the entire passenger seat.  I have the bucket seat slightly reclining back and this pet seat fits level, looks nice.

I was looking for a safety seat for my dog, and this is definitely NOT it. Doesn't come with any sort of belt or restraint, this is really just an expensive booster seat. If that's what you're looking for, I guess it's ok. It feels cheap for the price, and the colors were quite washed out compared to the bright plaid in the picture. I bought a harness and strap to attach to the seatbelt in my car, and my dog has no problem with it, and is safe. This chair looks ridiculous in the car and provides no additional safety.

I've had this product for a few months now.  I don't travel in my car as I regularly used to.  My dog hated being in the backseat and not being able to look out as she's very small.  Now, she gets in my car and jumps into the seat right away.  Its perfect for her to jump into and out of.  She is even comfortable sleeping in it after lengthy walks and playing with other puppies.

Previously, I had one of this doggie car seat. Finally I receive the right order and on time.Thank you  David  with the online Chat Customer Service for assisting me with your patient and professional attitude.

I returned this and got a small. The medium was much too big for my Yorkie/Papillon mix. Also huge in my car. The small fits her just right. Plenty of room to lay down, turn around, etc....since she started out riding in the car without a seat (big mistake on our part) there gas been quite an adjustment. She's normally a super quiet dog. But to begin with she barked and whined. We stuck to our guns and she is accepting it more and more. The hardest things was for US to accept it. Whoever is in the passenger would, for selfish reasons, prefer to cuddle her (she's so darn cuddly!).  But we know she is safer so we are being consistent and having her ride in her seat each time.
We have 2 and what a difference it made, it's made well and it SAFE! She can see out and she loves cars rides.

If you have a dog that rides in the car please buy one of these. I bought this along with the padded harness that attaches to the seatbelt for my 10 lb silky terrier.  Before having this car seat it was hard to keep my dog in the back seat while traveling.  She is small and would jump on the console and into my lab.  I know many people let their small dogs ride on their laps while driving, I was one in the past, but it is very risky.  If the airbag goes off it will injure or maybe even kill them.  I had never even though of this and once it was pointed out to me I make sure to spread the word. This car seat was the perfect solution.  My dog loves it and I actually think she likes it better than being in my lab. At first she was hesitant and whined a little but after the first couple of times she got used to it.  She can see out the window while sitting in the comfortable seat and after a long day to wherever we traveled she is always passed out and peacefully sleeping in it.  The storage compartment is very nice too.  I originally received one of the seats that hang from your seats car but exchanged it for the Snoozer Lookout II and couldn't be happier.  The previous hanging one looked like it would eventually break or tear up your car leather by pulling and rubbing on it.  This idea is much better and well worth the money.
We adapted a new cat, and since we needed a box to bring cat home bought this from Amazon.  Only fun fact is we went with a Male cat, and this is pink. Assembly was very easy and well made.

The holes on the front don't line up for the screws that are mandates by the airlines.  Someone screwed up in china.  Other than that it is ok.  I gave it to a friend and bought a different one because it was smaller than expected (my error) and I didn't want one of my fur babies to not be able to change positions for 23 hours.

I needed a travel crate for my new puppy to be flown from FL to NY, weighing in at 4 lbs. She had plenty of room and this travel crate has passed the test for durability. It's super cute and it is very durable. No problems whatsoever. Great purchase.

My kitty is 10 years old, and medium size. He fits perfectly inside, without a lot of extra room so he doesn't tousle around in the car. (That scares him) The top is held to the bottom by clips as you can see, but each clip has a slot for 'zip ties' so it won't accidentally snap apart if you are travelling.

My cats even like to go sleep inside it, if I leave the door open.They think of it as a refuge from noise, and maybe from each other.And getting them to think of it this way really makes it easy for transporting them whennecessary.  It doesn't look out of place in the Family Room, so often I have have put it in the cornerafter coming back from the vet's.  Invariably one of the cats will climb in an curl up.  This was a good buy!
Great carrier and great price.

I purchased for my two cats Duke & Chi Chi.  Duke is the kitten and Chi Chi is full grown and the both fit perfectly with room to spare.  It is a bit much to carry because with the two cats it is very heavy; however, I like the sturdiness of the Kennel Cab.

The clamps were secure and as I left the vet and approached my car, the bottom of the crate and the cat fell two feet to the ground and the Oskar Feralson flew around the parking lot, then under the car,  then into the engine of the car.  It is a major miracle that after many attempts, the vet was finally able to inject the angry cat and a very brave vet tech was able to remove a part of the engine and pull the drowsy cat free. I would never carry an animal in this crate again.

My 55-lb Chow Chow mix loves this bed. It's very light, and we travel a lot, so we take it with us everywhere. She always goes straight to it. It is quite thin, like other reviews have said, but our dog doesn't have orthopedic problems, so it's not a big deal for us. We do put a $5 moving blanket underneath it for extra padding and that does the trick for me. It fits in her dog crate, but we usually don't put it in there since she doesn't come off it much anyway.
This carrier bed is more plush than others I've purchased, and it looks very well made.  Fits into carrier perfectly.
Nice quality bed, seems pretty durable so far. Fits perfectly inside of a 42  crate. It's not the thickest bed in the world but is comfortable enough.

The bed is holding up after at least 6 months and my German Shepherds who are no longer puppies, still like it.  It seems a little thin compared to another bed that I bought them and seems to get dirtier, but all in all, a pretty good bed.
Our boxer loves this bed.  Washable and light weight.

Well one is a puppy one is big. My dogs seem to like these so far. We have a year old dog and a 3 month old pup both seem comfortable. The only draw back my wife sees is the size so far as fitting in the washing machine. We purchased a new larger crate and the larger of the two we brought fits perfect as does the other one in the slightly smaller crate.
Very nice pet beds for the price. Easy to toss in the washer and very durable. Fits perfectly in the metal crates.

We purchased this fleece bed when we purchased a dog crate, and when we got it, we were a little bummed to find how thin it was.  It was so flattened out that it was like having a fleece blanket.  Also, our dog is not one who will tear up a bed or pillow, but something about this fleece made him go a little batty - it's the only thing we have had to teach him not to tear up.  I don't know if it's the texture or what it is, but his initial instinct was destruction :)  We purchased a different bed that's slightly smaller & fits inside of this one, & we have a fleece blanket on top of that, & that works fine, but this was certainly not worth the money for our dog.
The bed is nice and comfortable. The problem is that my GSD tries to rip it out of his kennel and chews on it.  As he gets bigger, I am going to wish it had more padding.
My huge dog absolutely loves this bed.  He looks so adorable when he rests his big head on the edge and looks up at me.  This is definitely one of the most comfortable beds he's ever had.
The bed was delivered very quickly and in great condition. My dog seems to really like the bed and lays in it all the time.
This was a great bed for my dog, until he ripped it all up.  Good thing was that it's been the longest one that lasted out of all the other beds we've tried!
This bed while not the most comfortable is perfect for the cage. It is so easy to clean and dry. All you have to do it put it in the washer and voila.
My dog loves laying on this. We did not purchase it for a crate, we just put it on the floor w/ a blanket and he loves it. He is a great dane.

As soon as the bed was delivered, I placed it on the floor and my 3 month old puppy loved it immediately. She sits on it all the time. For me, I wished the bottom was just a little thicker but then again no complaints from my pup.

I'm dissapointed in this product.  It's not very padded, in fact almost no better than laying a blanke out on the floor for your dog.  also he's been chewing the fleece and it's coming off.  Disapointing.

We've tried several brands -- but it's the malt flavor of this particular one that our cats seem to tolerate.  The only suggestion I have is to update the photo of this item.  It now comes in a bright blue packaging with the name Sentry much larger than Petrodex - at first I thought I had the wrong item.

I was disappointed that my kitten doesn't like this flavor. I put some on his mouth and when he licks it he shakes his head and turns away. I'm going to have to try different flavors until I find one he will like before I start training him to accept teeth brushing.
This is great toothpaste for our cat because she loves the taste, but the brushes are a loss.  We use gauze to brush her teeth using this toothpaste and it works for us.
Ferrets love eating out of this thing. They don't make a mess.

Absolutely the best pet food dish around. I use these bowls in my parrots cages. Makes feeding them a breeze and the best part is it is impossible for them to dump the food bowls now. It would also work well with other pets. I must have for reduced mess!

I ordered this and it is twice the size of the one we had before! Ferrets love to tip their dishes and this solved our problems of food everywhere. So far they have not figured out how to untwist and remove the crock - which is good, I use these for food and water. They seem to drink more water now - I use a transparent 10 oz for water - it ensures they have fresh water daily - no more watter bottles for us!

I absolutely love these crocks.  You can put the mount anywhere in the cage.  It is super easy to put in and remove the crock, even when full of water or food.  And they are dishwasher safe for the most part.  Out of about 20 dishes, 2 were warped from the heat of the water.  Putting them on the top rack would've been smarter, perhaps.  Of course, washing by hand is extremely easy, too.
I bought 2 of these for my ferrets. They attach to the cage so no problems with them getting spilled. Not too big so they don't take a lot of space.
Great for shih tZu face where tears stain and my white dog

I bought this because a fellow Maltese owner suggested this. I do notice highlights in her fur. It's cheap enough where I would buy it again, and it does smell good. I would recommend although I am going to try some CC products.
This shampoo lathers really well and smells great.  My doggie's tan/white coat looks much brighter and is super soft just after 1 bath with this shampoo.  We love it and highly recommend it!
Mild yet effective. My dogs just love this. Leaves them nice and clean with no scratching after. Will reorder again.
My dog has allergies and this helps to a degree but not as much as I guess I thought it would,  But again it helps so give it a 4 and thanks,

I washed two dogs with this shampoo. One a long-haired daushound-corgi mix and the other a black lab mix.  Both coats were left shiny and fresh smelling (like from the groomers) after using this product. Producing 'Fresh n' Clean' results, as promised.The shampoo itself was gentle on my hands, but a bit more runny than expected (not thick or concentrated). The scent was not overpowering both when being used nor on the dogs after they were dry.I would consider this shampoo a low-suds formula, and it took quite a bit of it to get a good lather going on both dogs. The shampoo rinsed out with some effort, and did not leave their coats feeling particularly conditioned or soft. Upon drying, their coats felt soft though. I liked the shampoo, and the fresh scent didn't seem to bother the dogs at all. It seem to linger a bit, but not in a strong or harsh way.Why the drop in the star rating? You have to use quite a bit to get a lather going, and it doesn't easily rinse from the dog's coat. This formula is not a concentrate. The price seems high, but when you consider the amount your getting it's not a real issue. But the amount of it you have to use makes it go more quickly than if it were a thicker formulation.If that's an issue for you, consider one of Fresh n' Clean's other formulations that are 15-1 concentration.Fresh 'n Clean Oatmeal n' Baking Soda 15:1 Concentrate Shampoo, Tropical Breeze Scentmay be more to your liking.Overall, this is a good product in terms of its gentle cleansing power and fresh, long lasting scent. This bottle should last a long time, and with Aloe Vera in the mix, it should be a good choice for frequent bathing of your dogs if desired.

Our Soft Coated Wheaten Terrier is now nearly 16 years old and this shampoo has been a favorite throughout her long, happy life.  It maintains a gentle and pleasant scent from shampoo to shampoo.  A pleasing side effect of this shampoo is that she never gets that  wet doggy  smell due to the scent being revitalized once the coat becomes damp.Our dog is old now and has that unfortunate old dog smell syndrome so more frequent use is necessary.  The downside is that more frequent shampooing does dry her skin and cause flaking.  Fresh 'n Clean doesn't help much with the dry skin condition but the Lambert Kay Oatmeal and Baking Soda is a good alternative.I highly recommend the standard Fresh 'n Clean Shampoo.

I ordered this shampoo for my Wheaten as it was characterized as having a fresh clean scent that would last for a couple of weeks.  Well, I didn't particularly like the scent but my dog didn't seem to mind but that's a matter of opinion so I can't hold that against the product.  It did a good job of getting rid of the dirt which he always brings in when returning from a walk so that's a plus.  One minus point on this shampoo is the container -- it's just too big and clumsy to pour a small amount onto my dog.

I have a 7 year old Cavalier King Charles with really fine, fluffy fur. When it's long, it's super soft but tends to have a drier, wispier appearance than that of his siblings.I got this shampoo to review through the Vine program, and tried it out on him --This stuff is amazing! My mom, dad, sister, and some friends all noticed that my dog's fur seemed healthier and glossier than normal. I have to agree. He also smells wonderful. It's a fresh, clean scent that's slightly sweet. I love it.Sure, this stuff is a little expensive... but you get a GALLON of it, and it works really well.Especially for those of you with dogs who have finer / drier fur, I'd recommend giving this a shot. I got this first gallon for free but intend to purchase more once I run out. It's good stuff.
Excellent! I've never used a dog shampoo so long lasting and the scent is very nice. So subdued but lovely. The dogs seem to like it to and they run around smelling each other. Love it!

My dog likes to wrestle with her dog cousins - in the dirt. She also likes to hoof it through whatever  mess  she can. (why they like to do this is beyond me).I'd been using an oatmeal shampoo that had little fragrance, but she seemed to need a bath more frequently than I was willing to go with her.This Fresh n' Clean Scented Shampoo is really nice. It comes in a huge jug so you may want to dispense it into smaller containers for regular use - but that's nothing.The shampoo keeps her fur soft and smooth and WOW the fragrance - if well rinsed - is not overpowering but is certainly welcomed and fresh and clean smelling (just as the name states). It's a bit like having her been run through the dryer with Bounce sheets (lots of them).  It's that kind of smell.However, you need to mindful to really rinse your dog as the cream rinse consistency can cling and while it doesn't hurt the dog or you - the fragrance can be overpowering.The nice thing is the fragrance lasts - her latest bath - the fragrance is still there two weeks later.Loving that!

Lambert Kay's Fresh and Clean shampoo has been around for as long as I can remember, over 25 years. There is nothing faddish or gimmicky about it. It cleans as it advertises, and left my dogs coat soft and shiny. We call him  Mr. Stinky,   sometimes, he just needs a bath every two weeks. I diluted the shampoo with water (about 1:5 ratio) in an empty dish detergent bottle before I soaped him up, this lathers up nicely, I put shampoo exactly where I want it, and it rinses out easily. It does make him smell good! Props to Lambert Kay for being American made AND Employee owned.The shampoo is ph balanced for your dogs skin. I will say my hands felt a little drier than usual after using this shampoo, compared to other ones I like. As a groomer, I buy in bulk, and have tried many shampoos. I'll confess I prefer the currant brand I use, Espree, to this one. I think it smells nicer and does contain natural/organic ingredients, and leaves my hands less dry.

Ok...I was SO excited to get this product, and after using it, I'm even more excited.  It actually works!!!We have a Golden Retriever, he is a smelly thing, we give him a bath and he smells within hours.  I have tried many shampoos, remedies and nothing has worked, not until I received the Fresh 'n Clean Scented Shampoo.It's been about 2 weeks since his last bath and he's still smelling good....simply amazing, I may just buy an entire case of this stuff.It smells a bit strong if you sniff the jug, but once on the dog, it's not strong at all...maybe there's a secret potion in the scent...I don't care what it is, IT WORKS!!!Definitely recommend this product.

This is our first time trying this dog shampoo.The strong, synthetic, fake fragrance smell (like cheap dryer sheets) knocked me over on opening the bottle.We have a very large dog so buying shampoo by the gallon is nice for us.This shampoo seemed pretty running and we used more than we normally do with our current favorite shampoos (HyLyt Moisturizing and Earthbath Oatmeal/Aloe).The lather was average and the shampoo did a very good job of removing the dirt from our dog's thick coat.He didn't scratch or itch afterwards and he smelled  fresh like a dryer sheet  when done.  If you like that smell you will probably like this product.We gave it away to a friend with 3 dogs and she loves it (scent and all).

I have a 10 pound dog who doesn't shed his fur so he requires regular trimmings.As a result, his hair can get very oily. I found that if I dilute the shampoo to 15 parts of water per 1, the shampoo is too watery to create lather. So I dilute it less (a lot less), and it works great to clean his fur. He smells so great after a doggy bath! The scent is only there though for 1-2 days, then he's back to his old self again.The instructions state to not to dilute to help detangle matted fur/tangles. His fur get matted sometimes and the undiluted version is great for detangles, but not so much for matted fur. The only cure for matted fur is to simply trim off the matted fur, and to brush constantly to prevent the fur from getting matted again.For those that shed and don't need brushing, this product does the job.  For those that don't shed and need trims, like yorkies, this stuff is good but it could be a little better. The fact that you can dilute this means that it will last you quite a while, which is great if you have multiple dogs.

When I first tried this shampoo on my dogs, I was not at all happy with the smell. Quite frankly, during the bathing process, the smell is a little creepy, a little like cigarette smoke and shampoo. However, once it dries, it has a quite pleasant smell and it lasts for a long time. Since they sleep on my bed, I usually bathe my dogs weekly. They still smell good at the end of a week. As an added bonus, their fur is much softer. My female dog is a poodle mix and her fur is a little stiff; after using this shampoo, her fur is much softer and less wiry. My maltipoo's fur is as soft as ever.It lathers more than any other dog shampoo I've ever used, and it seems like the gallon bottle will last a long time.I do use a different shampoo on their faces, since I do not believe this is tear-free.

I really love this dog shampoo.  Molly's long hair has always been a problem after a shampoo (with baby shampoo).  Hair on her legs was always tangled, and she whined while I was attempting to brush the tangles out.  With this shampoo there were no tangles, just smooth and shiny hair.  She looks just great!What I didn't like as much is the fact that, for me, it seems to be a low suds shampoo.  Now I don't count on suds to do the cleaning, but the suds allow me to judge when I've rinsed all the shampoo out.  This time I rinsed probably twice as long as with other shampoos.There's plenty of shampoo in this gallon jug, enough to see Molly through the end of her lif, and I will be using it for however long it lasts.  I think it's great, and I can recommend it for other dog owners.  I think you'll like it as much as I do.FIVE STARS!

Original Review: I tested this on a very allergic corgi/chihuahua, while I had a cut on my thumb.  The initial smell is fairly overpowering:  I found it difficult to tolerate while washing her. It does rinse off pretty well, and the scent it leaves is faint and not-offensive.However, this particular shampoo didn't change much of the scratching my dog is doing, so I'm not sure I'd use it again.  It didn't make her scratching worse, but a fairly serious wash-and-rinse with this did not seem to help her allergies much.On the plus side, it also didn't aggravate or harm the cut I had on my own thumb. It's not a very strong detergent, which is a plus if you're trying to bathe a dog with scrapes and cuts on your hands.Edit: One week after I used this shampoo, my dog was rubbing her face, chewing her paws, and chewing her tail.  I washed her with her regular Crazy Dog shampoo, and used a medicated shampoo with chlorhexidine on her paws and tail, to get rid of any bacteria.It's been two days since I switched her back to her regular shampoo combination, and I've caught her licking her paw, once.This is not a good shampoo for allergic dogs.

The scent of this shampoo is nice but after washing with it, the scent is gone by day two.  I normally use human head and shoulders on my dogs, and the scent stays for up to a week.  This did seem to get my two dogs clean, they just didn't keep that clean doggy smell for very long. Also the large container was unwieldy while trying to pin a puppy into the tub, and get the right amount on the dog without dumping out half the bottle. Had this come with a normal soap dispenser type pump I would have been much happier.  Perhaps they assume that everyone has a pump to use for this - I didn't.  I did like the larger size and the scent, I just wish the dogs had remained smelling fresh and clean for longer.

Fresh ’n Clean shampoo is good, basic shampoo for dogs.  We have two dogs in our household, a young short haired dog and an elderly longer haired dog who suffers from all kinds of skin allergies and itching.  Fresh ’n Clean works well for them both.  Our elderly pup still itched after his bath, but perhaps slightly less.  Bathing him with a shampoo containing Aloe Vera makes me feel a little better, anyway.The scent is pleasant and really does last a long time.  Even weeks after, I caught a slight whiff of it when the dog wet his fur from licking himself.The 1 gallon size is convenient, but also a problem.  Trying to handle a gallon jug while corralling a dog who doesn’t want a bath can be a challenge.  Also with the gallon size, it’s easy to pour out a lot more than you really need, wasting shampoo.  A pump is a good idea if you’re going with the gallon jug.Nice, long-lasting scent; easy on my elderly pup’s itchy skin and a fair price with free shipping.  5 stars

I like the scent of this product - it is the same shampoo scent radiating from my dogs after a trip to Groomingdales.  However, the product that I received was not the shampoo, but rather the cream rinse.  I have 2 small Yorkies and two larger dogs that do not have long hair, so I don't see myself putting a dent in this gallon bottle anytime soon.  One of my Yorkies has to be bathed weekly due to an overabundance of oil in her skin, so when I used it on her, she came from her bath smelling great, but pretty greasy within a couple days, so I probably won't be using it on her again.  The other Yorkie took to it just fine.Just a little disappointed - was really hoping for the shampoo.
If you want your dog to smell like a old man that wears a brute cologne, then this is the perfect product. This cologne is not for me, but the smell does last long.
Great big bag - enough for 7 cats - lasts months !Excellent supplement for cats who prefer homemade cat food ... Great for cat eyesight protection !

Do not mess with oil that you canj't trust that might gunk up your clippers. This oil is great. It lubes up the blades and a little bit goes a long way. This keeps your blades and equipment lasting longer and that is worth a few extra bucks.Enjoy
Bought this for my dogs' razor blade to cut their hair.  Small and simple and good price and keeps the blades oiled.

I decided to buy this product on line simply because it was much cheaper than buying it at the pet store.  I've had my Oster 76 Classic for more than 10 years and it still works like a charm.  The secret......maintenance and keep the blades clean and lubricated before, during, and after use.

I tasted it to see how powerful it is. It's very powerful. So far the dogs have not chewed the carpet, our shoes, or anything other than their very own toys. Gonna need a lot more and, hopefully, in a much larger size.

My cat was having an episode of aggressive marking the apartment door, I started spraying this and he wouldn't go near anymore. Really helped me set him on the right track again. After a few days I needed less and less product.

We have a new puppy and since we already had this for our cat (who is now older and not a problem), we thought to try it on places we didn't want the dog scratching or digging.  It worked just fine!  There are dog ones on the market, too, but this seemed to work fine for us and if it is safe for cats, we assume it is safe for dogs.

it does smell horrible, i'm sure that's the whole point. I've gotten it on my hands before, didn't eat through the skin (the warning label on it scares you), but I did wash good with soap and hot water. As soon as the smell goes away, my cat is right back at it! So definately don't think you can spray in the morning and when you come back from work your cat wouldn't have been putting his/her claws where they don't belong!!! Next time I'll try another product.

Like other reviewers have mentioned, you have to keep spraying the same area in order for it to be effective, which I find highly annoying. I sprayed the area around my memory foam mattress as I have a naughty cat who has a habit of putting her nails into it. I just wished it lasted longer and didn't smell so bad.
I used this on a screen door, that has lattice work on the bottom, and it would work until it dried, then the cat would be right back there, climbing.  I wouldn't recommend this product.

I gave it 2 stars because it doesn't lie: it repels cats. Unfortunately, after only a few sprays I had to open all the doors and windows, light a candle, burn incense and hope I wouldn't throw up. My cats hid under the bed. I tried to find a reason to leave the house. It was almost comical. At least it was only 5 bucks.

I did not give this 5 stars for two reasons.  One (and most importantly to me) whenever I spray it the spray seems to get all over my finger.  My cat wont come near me even after I wash my hands profusely once it's dribbled down my spraying finger.  The other reason is it doesn't last very long (which I'm not sure can be remedied and am not weighing very heavily compared to the finger getting drenched point).Other than that, this stuff is great.  It smells a lot like cilantro so I don't mind it.  There might be an ever so slight kind of hidden Ammonia after-smell under-tone thing going on, but overall it's like 95% cilantro and unless I sit there huffing the scent of it after having just sprayed that's all I notice is Cilantro.  The cat definitely doesn't like the stuff,  it doesn't last long but it's pretty effective for training.  She will avoid the spot for a couple hours usually.  I will usually put several paper towels in the sink and get them all nice and wet, then put the paper towels in the areas I don't want her to sit (namely my kitchen table & chairs and on my bed). Third - and I probably should have mentioned this first: The picture is so unbelievably misleading!! You will not receive three packages that are packaged as appears in the picture. First off, note that the 30L rating is the  expanded  measurement.  I've used just about every brand of shredded paper bedding material over the last couple of years for my son's hamster. Frequent changing and maintenance does much more for odor control than brand choice.Compared to the white or colored beddings, the brown is a bit more rough and less fluffy, but it is also cheaper.  That said, it doesn't retain its fluff quite as well as the white or colored bedding.  If you look at the compressed vs. expanded ratings on the bags, the white and colored beddings advertise a lower fluffed volume for the same size compressed volume.  The trade off is that they are softer and retain their fluff better.  Would I buy this again?  Definitely - I've used it in the past and will continue to buy it.  Am I brand loyal? This is a great test. It's easy to use and one kit will give you several months of tests.The test itself is very straightforward using a method called titration: add drops from bottle 1, shake, then add drops from bottle 2 until the solution turns from pink to the purple color indicated on the instructions. In-between drops from bottle 2, you invert the tube with the cap securely on. The more drops you need from bottle 2, the more calcium you have. You check the back of the instructions to translate number of drops to ppm.  I have been keeping SPS, LPS, softs, and calcium-reliant macro algae in a small (25 gallon) system for some time with this kit and have had no calcium problems.As a quick tip: if you have multiple tests you run in beakers, get a 100cc syringe and attach some airline hose to the end. That way, you can fill the syringe with about 30cc of tank water and squirt it into each beaker to get the perfect amount in each (usually 5cc). No more dipping beakers in your tank and pouring some out, refill, pour out, refill, etc. Just put in 5cc directly and voila!Mine came with instructions and everything I needed. I have had no problems using this. Note that, the higher your calcium levels, the more drops from bottle 2 it will take and, thus, the fewer total tests you will get from this kit.
