Never bought this before and thought it might be good in a pinch when I have no time to cook for my dogs. I am pretty picky about what they eat and this was a mistake. I threw it away after reading all the ingredients.

I was looking for an economical but healthy way to make training treats for my dogs, and it looked like this would be the answer. I cut it up into small cubes and they did seem to like the flavor. Well, no wonder! Sucrose is one of the main ingredients. I guess it's a way to condense a lot of calories into a small amount of space, which might be a good idea for working dogs or very active dogs, but not for my guys. Plus, I don't relish the idea of brushing their teeth after every training session or snack.

The value here is high compared to other training treats like Zukes. These are great to make any size you want, or they can nibble off a little at a time as you are training. I cut up and refrigerate it in a container.

I wanted to try the Chicken and Liver Food Roll.  Unfortunately, they sent me the Lamb and Rice roll instead.  The dog loves it, but  I think it is too crumbly to be a real handy treat.  I wonder if the Chicken and Liver Food Roll would have been better.

I bought this to use as training treats for two dogs. Both got sick. Terrible diarrhea that got so bad that we had to bring one to the vet to the tune of $250. I knew there was all kinds of crap in this that I normally wouldn't dream of feeding my dogs, but I thought they would be getting so little of it and I wanted something different from the everyday fare. Save your money. Boil a chicken and use the meat for treats and the broth (minus the fat) as a protein supplement with their kibble. Buying this was one major screw up!

We originally purchased the hive that came with the bees last year for a Christmas present for the boys, the dogs had no interest in playing hide and go seek with the hive but the bees were a big hit and have lasted a year through the abuse of 3 dogs, 1 chihuahua, 1 Maltese And 1 Havanese.These are the perfect size for small to medium sized dogs though I would not recommend them for larger breeds as they would most likely tear them apart right away.The wings give something for the dog to hold on to when they fetch it or the head as they are just the right size. I highly suggest buying them here and from this company as the shipping was just as perfect as the product.
I bought these for our dog and he loved them. Tough but soft,durable and he enjoys making them pop and squeak.
When offered my cat prefers eating out of this than his bowl :) And he's loosing weight! I never have food on the carpet, he gobbles it all up!

fits an entire packet of treat (so you don't have to keep it around) and the different sizes of the holes the food comes out is a great idea - I started with wide open to entice both cats to play with it - a little while later I dropped the size to half - and they still played with it - but it took them longer to get the treats and now that only 1 cat is interested in it - I put it down to the smallest hole so she really has to work for a treat - keeps her happy for hours. Great toy - can be washed.

Very nice variation of size in the different holes.  You could use all sizes of treats in this one and also still have the ability to adjust to size you need.  Sometimes the ball slides itself and opens the holes more, but not too bad.  Kitties love it when I fill it and give it to them.

This ball is ok if you have the right sized treats. The treats that I have are too big for the small holes, but too small for the big holes. They came pouring out all at once. My cat doesn't have too much interest in it. I think it's too big and he doesn't even realize that it's a toy. Maybe once I find the right combination of treats. I will keep trying!

The vet told us that our male cat was overweight, and we should look into a cat food ball that he has to work to get food out of, instead of just letting him snarf as much food as he wants from their bowl. This is what we got. It took the cats a few days to figure it out, but now they seem to have the hang of it. If nothing else, it's much more entertaining to watch them eat this way. We're feeding them Iam's Indoor Weight and Hairball Care, which has very small kibbles. There are a lot of settings to adjust the rate the food comes out, but I do wish there were even more: because the kibble is so small it's hard to find a setting between  nothing comes out  and  food comes out with very little effort .

My cat is not overweight but I thought she'd enjoy this. Turns out she doesn't want to eat her food off the carpet. Despite her personal preference, I thought the idea of this was great but the design is terrible. The locking mechanism is flimsy and concerns me as a choking hazard, even if you're supervising your cat (as you should) while using it. The ball itself looks like if my cat was interested in it she would easily break it. Additionally, the openings in the ball that you can adjust to (in theory) effect how much food can fall out leaves a lot to be desired and you will likely find that your only options are to have next to no food coming out or to have way too much coming out.I'd like to expand my review on the openings in the ball because looking at the picture, it may be deceiving. There are six openings in the ball, not including the large screw top where you open it to put in the food. Three of the openings are shield-shaped like the picture shows, and the other three are ovals. When you twist the ball you change how much of these opening are covered. The problem is if the opening is the right size for the shield-shaped holes, it's probably too big for the ovals and vice versa. This leads to making it next to impossible to have the ball dispense food the way you'd want it to.

I bought two of these a few months ago -- one for me and one for a friend.  My 15 month old male cat loves his ball.  He didn't have a problem with eating so fast and then getting sick but he would definitely eat and overeat.  Plus, I had a habit of filling the bowl up too much.  This ball serves exactly one cup which is their daily allowance. I think he has lost a half pound in the few months he's been on it and I think this will help him live along and healthy life.  Usually I fill it half way twice daily.  I've even filled it all the way and he paces what he eats (there will be some left over the next day).  A few downsides:  If your cat is ball crazy, mine is, -- he may play with this even when he's not hungry and leave bits a food on your floor.  Also, it's a bit noisy and if you live in a small apartment you can hear it (in the middle of the night, etc).  Speaking of size, I love that it's small and doesn't take up room on my counter.  I'm about to adopt a 2nd cat so I'm getting a second ball that might be an interesting dynamic.

My cats not interest in this thing at all. He likes food, loves snacks and string but this thing does absolutely nothing for him.Lastly, you get 2 cents worth of plastic and they charge $5.00 bucks for it?? I was duped.

I do like it and its a great idea, but i bought only one with two cats thinking they would play together with it like they do with everything else.  They do everything together.  But this toy, they started to fight over it with growling because it contains food, so I stopped using it. I suppose I could get another but not sure if I will.

So, I have quite possibly one of the most adorable/gorgeous cats ever--but she is definitely not very bright, at all..  She has a tendency to sometimes eat her food too quickly and throw up.  Because she's on the lean side and could stand to gain a little weight if anything, I didn't want to withhold food at any time, so I thought this could be good; especially considering she won't even touch wet food.Well, I showed her how to use it many times.. so many times.  I really didn't think she'd ever learn how to use it.  She'd eat the food that came out when I nudged it enough to release food, but nothing after that.But then, nearly two weeks later I came home for the day and saw that the ball had been moved a few feet!  (I had been leaving it in the same spot on purpose).  Over the next week she got better at using it.  She still hasn't quite mastered moving it with her paw, and instead uses her head.. but ah well.  And she still gets 'stuck' whenever she pushes the ball into the corner and can't get it to move.  But I think she's getting better.  She seems to like it, and even prefers eating from it, versus the food in her bowl (in which I still always leave a bit of food), odd, which is still good I guess.Anyway, even if your cat doesn't understand it right away, don't give up hope.

I love that this comes in different colors, it is dishwasher safe, and easy to use. However the shape makes it super easy for the cat to eat. Since it is a ball there is nothing to stop the toy from rolling. Also my cat's food is very small so the ball rolls and everything comes out in a straight line on the floor. (yes I have the setting as small as it will go).  I've also purchased the egg-cersizer meal toy. Compared to that toy the wholes in the slim cat are smaller. For the most part I like the idea of this toy as it entertains my cat during his meals.

boy i wanted our cat to be able to use this thing but she could not for the life of her figure out how to roll the darned thing and i left no other food out.  so that's not the fault of the product that our sweet kitty is dumber than dirt.. (not sure i would love having food scattered on the floor but if a regular cat would use it, i'm sure they would snarf up the food)

The idea of this is good, but the holes are larger than the food and treats my cats eat so they fall out really easily and a lot at a time. The point of this for me was to avoid 1 of my cats eating too fast, so that didn't work.

This is great for limiting the amount of food your cats get and still making them work for it.  It keeps my female cat from inhaling her food.  There was a bit of a learning curve when I first put these down, and I think one should be prepared to sit with the cats for a while to show them how the ball works.  These balls would be especially handy for someone who has cats that eat their dry food too quickly and need some regulation.  You can adjust the size of the dispensing holes, so most dry foods will work with this product.

I have two chubby cats who scarf their food down so fast, they throw up. This has helped them pace their meals and I notice they are actually eating less. It took a good few days for them to get used to the balls but now I actually think they enjoy them. Even my incredibly stubborn kitty bats the ball around with no issues!
My cats really love this and play with it for a long time. I have 13 cats who are not free fed as some are overweight thereforethis is really fun for them, but only a few can figure it out.

Durable, good size, easy to adjust size of holes and thus the frequency of treat dispensing. Also, unscrews to make it easy to get treats in and out.There is a small slide button that  locks  the hole opening to a certain size, and it often doesn't stay locked, so often when I find the toy, the holes are either fully open or fully closed (which really makes my pets mad!). But, it's still a great toy.I actually use this with my toy size dog. Very durable.
My cat could care less about this toy. She smelled it once and never played with it. My six year old was more fascinated with this toy. Just created more mess for me.

My cats grew tired of it quickly, and i have a rescue ranch with plenty of various personalities to try out toys on. It works as stated, however.  I think you might have to train your kitty to use it.  With so many cats here I didn't have time to train on this item.

I do not know what to rate this toy.  BUT I REALLY LIKE THIS TOY.  THIS TOY CAN GO IN THE DISHWASHER!!  There are multiple size holes on this, so you can give multiple difficulty levels OR multiple size treats from little kibbles to [like Feline Greenies smartbites or equlivalent (have smooshie center)] .  I put a size treat that was just about the size to fit through the largest hole [broke off piece of freeze dried liver YUM].  There is a screw off portion of the hole for humans to easily bulk enter kibbles, eg, if you decide to put all the cat food for the day into the ball (this would only work if you had a solo cat household, right?, but I don't think you could pack it full, because then the food couldn't roll around & then the kitty couldn't get the food out really).This toy is too big for the cats, though the plastic is lightweight.  It is almost as big as my kitty's heads'.  For kitty's who are more treat motivated, this may be okay, however, but my kitties are not so treat motivated, and I hate to admit, not that clever.  :(  have to be honest though.  Will update the post if I can get the kitties more treat motivated.  I have never found that any cats of mine like very large toys though.My DOG really likes toys like this though, so since it was mail order and not very expensive, I thought I would let my German Shepherd have a go at it.  So I put small squares of freeze dried liver so they could fall out the large hole.  She already knows how to roll toy around to get food out from another toy she has.  I didn't watch her but this was more challenging because the other toy has a slit all the way around (it's like a UFO and the food can come out all the sides), but this one the food can only come out the tiny hole.  So I thought she would be busy for a while.  So I turned my back on her & did something else & thought she would stay busy while figuring it out.  I don't know how she did it, but instead of rolling the food out the holes, she unscrewed the part that humans are supposed to unscrew to add the food.UPDATE:  I just had her retry it and she did it properly and it took more time and the screw part stayed on LOL!!!  I must have not screwed it on properly (I cannot rule out that she did not unscrew it with her nose, her nose is kind of like an elephant trunk it is very weird).  Probably is dog proof not HUMAN PROOF!  If your dog is not very gentle it is not good dog toy, my GSD is quite gentle but this plastic is very lightweight, I think they did try to design it for cats but I think smaller design for cats and keep it  snacky  only for half a meal maybe for cats.
This thing rolled away a long time ago. I put treats in it and my lazy cat couldn't care less. Guess my cat is just well fed and lazy.

I bought this on a Vet's recommendation which in theory seemed like a good idea to help with my pudgy cat.  Although the theory is great for some reason Sootie doesn't play with it even though there is food in it.  I gave it 4 stars as I liked the idea but Sootie wasn't thrilled about it which should be no reflection on the product.  Any person familiar with cats would understand.

My original review was that my cats wouldn't play with it. I kept showing them food dropping from it, and pushing it around, and eventually one cat got it. It took about five days, but he's figured out that if he plays with it, the food drops out. My other cat was a bit more stubborn, but this morning, after about an hour of showing him a couple pieces of food, and then putting the ball on top so he had to push the ball to get the food he knew was there, he figured out the ball was giving him food. It took about another hour for him to figure out the food didn't just magically appear there while he sat staring at the ball, and now he understands he has to push it to get the food.Like I said, it took about a week total for my cats to figure this out. Maybe they're just really dumb, but if your cats don't use it right away, don't despair. I had to take away their food all last night, which I'm sure helped them finally understand the ball is the only way they're gonna get food.I raised my review to 4 stars, and bought another one so they both have a ball. I didn't give it five stars because I do feel the latch mechanism is a little weak, and I think if you have to adjust it too many times it'll break pretty quick.

I have had no problems with getting it to work or getting my cats to use it.  But I had hoped it would encourage more play.  I had hoped they would be chasing it all over the house and attacking it.The cats just tap it to get out a few bits of kibble, eat the kibble and then tap it again.  But it does cut down on gorging and vomiting.
This is great for cat fun.  Making them work a bit for their treats is OK however I would NOT use this to feed them their whole meal.

This does not dispense the treats a bit at a time as the opening is difficult to adjust.  However, once the treats are gone, the cats continue to enjoy batting it around a bit - just in case one is still there.
I actually bought this not as a cat toy but as a way for my cats to loose weight. It works very well because they only get a certain amount each day and they have to try to get the food.

My cats were too lazy for this but I use it as a treat dispensing toy (actually a dinner dispensing toy) for my dog!  I love the adjustment for hole size - I started out making it easy for him but as he got more used to the toy, I made the holes smaller to challenge him :)

I have two cats and neither was interested in this toy.  I put their favorite treats in it and still...nothing.  It's a well made product and the idea is good...I don't really understand why they didn't like it....but it now sits ignored in a corner of our living room.
This is great in concept and I'm sure that a lot of other cats would love it but mine just can't figure it out.  Not a mensa candidate is she. lol!

I first put treats in the ball and just have a small holes open and food would drop out and my cat chased it like crazy around the kitchen. He got tired of chasing after his treats and nothing coming out, so I opened up the holes to the bigger size and the treats just dropped out so now sometimes if the treats are harder to come out of the small holes big holes they just fall out of so it's an okay toy first I thought he would love it but it's alright
Design - you can adjust it to dispense via 3 smaller holes or 3 larger holes, holds a good amount of kibble, and you can adjust easily.Cat learned to use it fairly quickly.

This ball is roughly the size of a tennis ball, it's made of hard blue plastic. The idea is you fill it with treats, adjust the slots so that the food/treat trickles out while your cat bats it around. I had a hard time getting the slots aligned so my Percy' s treats just wouldn't fall out everywhere. We use Pounce treats, the heart shaped dental cleaning treats. He could smell the treat, he wanted the treat, he even licked it a few times and that was it. It sat in my floor for a week full of yummy treats without any interest from him. I even showed him  multiple times how to get the treat out. My kid's thought I was crazy for sitting in the floor with the cat playing with a treat ball trying to school him in how to use it. I was hoping this toy would keep him from going stir crazy when we have bad weather and he can't go out on our enclosed deck. It seems very sturdy, and well constructed, but it just didn't interest my kitty. He'd rather play with my son's angry birds or my yarn.

I do not care for this product for the use it was advertised for.  The treats are extremely tiny to insert into Busy Buddy Toys--even the small ones.  The treats fall out immediately.  I didn't want to waste our money so I give the treats to our dogs with training sessions.

I bought these to go in the Busy Buddy Twist N Treat dog toy.. He likes the taste, but he can't seem to manuver the toy.. He's a dachshund and I think his little legs can't manuver it very well. So basically, these aren't working the way we wanted them to, but he does like the taste of them.
Picky Pomeranian here. Bought a treat ball dispenser with very small holes. These treats fit in nice and fall out easily. And Mr. picky LOVES them.

I bought these treats to put in a couple different treat dispensers and was very disappointed when they came. They're very small, so they don't work well in the treat dispensers I have. Way too much comes out at once. My dog does like the taste of them, but because they're so small, it's easy for him to miss some of them when they come out. Next time I'll stick to in store purchases so I can see the size before buying.

I was looking for something to put inside a couple of treat dispensing toys I have for my 3 Pomeranians.  When I got these, to my surprise, the treats looked like something to feed a mouse.  These are TINY treats and they don't fit into any of the multiple treat dispensing toys I have.  Well, they fit IN, but they come OUT almost immediately.  These are WAY too small.  Plus, so many of them were broken inside the bag when I got them that there was a bunch of powder in the bag.  Lastly, my dogs weren't even interested in the treats that fell on the floor.  I don't recommend this product.  Try something else.

We use these in our dogs' puzzle toys and Kongs, as they are a nice, small size, and fall out of the toys' various-sized openings well. I would recommend for anyone looking for treats to use in puzzle toys.
These tiny treats are the perfect size for a treat ball or a puzzle toy.  Even my Chi can get it on the play now that we have treats he can eat as well!

I know these are to put IN dog play toys but I have fun taking a handful and dropping them around the house and telling the two dogs when they come in from outside to  go hunt  and they go looking for them!! It is so fun for them (and me to watch) since I know it helps them learn to hunt and use their sniffers. These treats are a new addition to the indoor winter activities :)PS I do also use inside Busy Buddy holder toys.
A little expensive (4.5oz) , and for a large breed active dog, they don;t last long, BUT they are made in the USA and not China :)

These are great for training or putting inside busy balls.  I don't know if Cheerios would be the same or not, but they sure look the same and are probably cheaper.  That said, I thought they were much better than the smaller treats sold for the same purpose by the same company.  My dog loves them!
My Dog loves these! She is a fan of cheerios, so these being a healthier alternative is awesome, I'm sure all dogs would enjoy them, even the pickiest of eaters.
Good treats, they fit perfect in all dog toys and he loves them. Even the cat likes these treats, he will follow the dog with his toy around just to catch any missed treats on the floor.

Might as well use Cherrios or puffed rice. I am disappointed in most of the purple Busy Buddy treat toys. I really don't think my dogs are that dumb, but using them for treat toys is really challenging. They do much better with other toys and puzzles, so I do not think I will get these again. Do the dogs like them? You bet. My dogs like darn near everything.
I put these in my dogs toys and they love them. The fact that they play with it to eat them means they are exactly what i wanted.

I work with a rescue group A Rotta Love Plus and Bessie loves them. I have had no poop problems. I mixed these about 50/50 with her dog food in a play puzzle toy.  I like that they are crisp even after several weeks.
My dog is in love with this bone. Will spend long periods of time munching away and then will leave it for a bit as they go through these pretty fast and she wants it to last!
Nothing super special about this rawhide.  The dog liked it, but it didn't seem to last as long as some other types.
This lasted 2 weeks for my aggressive chewer German Shepherd. My dog can finish a rawhide in about 2-3 hours. I bought this at Menards for 7$ which is less than half the price here.
Bought these for my mutts. They seemed to really like them... They were gone in a couple days. I like the rawhides with the knots on the ends, takes them longer to chew through.
This matches the pictures in the listing.  It is a bit unwieldy for my Bernese Mountain dog but that is part of the fun for her.

This was not the quality of big, long, thick bone I've purchased for my dog in the past that kept him occupied for weeks.  This one has only a fold or two of rawhide and Blaze tore though it in a day and about the same price as the much better quality bones I've bought in the past.
We put them in the Everlasting Wheeler and our dogs spend many happy hours chewing away!Quiet time in the evening for the humans.

These treats last longer thn any others I have ever tried. Even my tough chewer...and I do mean tough, normally shreds or eats anything we give her within 10 minutes. This treat can take hours...sometimes days, because they just last so long before they are all chewed up.Yay!

These seem to be well liked by my Golden Retreiver but they are not long lasting chews. It was gone after about 20 minutes and dog seemed to choke on the last piece as it swallowed the piece once it got down to where he could just swallow what was left. Also left stain marks on the carpet. So I will not be re-ordering these, only because of the choking hazard.

I buy these often for my dogs.  The medium is the perfect size for my mini schnauzer and puggle (pug/beagle).  These really do last a long time.  They work with the StarMark Everlasting treat holders.  I have the diablo (pink/orange) ones that look something like top spinners.  One word of caution: they take a little elbow grease to fit into the holders, so these are not ideal for someone with severe arthritis or other wrist/hand challenges.  For someone with strength issues, I would recommend my second-favorite long-lasting treat: busy bones.
This was a new flavor for our dog and she seemed to enjoy it. She loves to chew and chew until she gets them out of her ball.

These are really awesome! Dog loves these things, but as I wrote in my 'medium/chicken' review I only let him chew on it for 30 mins at a time, otherwise his slobber loosens up the treat and it disinigrates much faster. So only letting him have it for 30 mins gives us many, many, many 30 min turns, versus if I just let him go at it for two hours the thing is nearly gone. I use a screw driver to pop it in and out really easy without ruining my manicure. I give the left over wafers to my friend who has a really small dog that chews them up, so none is wasted!  And to be honest, I bought the large on accident, but since I didn't have a bento ball yet (I had the small one for him as a tiny puppy, which he loved) I bought a large bento ball. I found that the regular large holder was gigantic (in person at the store), but the large bento ball for some reason not so much and is just fine for our 6 month old golden retriever. Plus he loves that I can put his kibble in the back for extra fun.
good taste, loves to lick until there is a whole in the center.  definitely cheaper here than in the pet store.  a must purchase.

These are made from beef liver, my dog is allergic to poultry and eggs and all the local stores only carry chicken flavored Everlasting Treats. I use these in the Everlasting Bento Ball. My dog found the treats good for a casual chew, but not so exciting that he felt the need to protect them from the other pets. Without the ball the treats last a good 15-20 minutes. With the ball he was working on it for a week.
This is GREAT for your pet.  If your pet is smart enough it will take it out of its package.
Our three Malamutes love these and eat them up in no time.  However,  Everlasting Treat . . .  it absolutely is NOT.  Maybe 15 minutes . . .

Although I generally aviod treats and toys that are not sourced and manufactured in the USA, out of safety concerns (lots of dogs dying from certain brands of dog treats from China), I have to recommend this line.We have a couple of the Starmark toys that hold these treats.Both dogs love them. One is an aggressive chewer with jaws that could crush rocks, the other smaller and more delicate. Both enjoy them, and they are absolutely the longest lasting treats I have ever found (constant searching for the super-chewer has provided much experience here).Be aware that the treats (like all treats) are to be supervised, and these are recommended for use inside one of the toys, so that big chunks are much less likely to be swallowed, which could cause big problems.When the dogs get bored with a flavor I take a little cheese and mush it all around the remaining treat and edges of the toy where the treat portion touches it. They generally find it very interesting again, as if it were a new treat.Occasionaly I take it out and insert it backwards. Giving a new and differnt surface, and sometimes take it out, switch with a different flavor, and keep the original one for a new switch-out.You had better get one for each dog, or there will be war.

Our dogs both love the starmark balls and insert treats, but for some reason this is the favorite flavor.We notice no unpleasant odor, even when the dogs have been chewing for a while.The price may seem high, but this treat is the longest lasting type they have ever had.Everything else is eaten or forgotten pretty quickly.I only use them inside the starmark treat toys, and have had no issues with indigestion or intestinal problems.I normally buy only dog food/treats sourced and made in the USA, but this is an exception.I wish there were Made in USA products that lasted as long, but I have not found any yet. :(At any rate, 2 thumbs waaay up on these long lasting and economical treats.
My three little ones simply love these treats.  I tried the size small, but they disappeared too quickly.  These ones last much longer, and don 't leave any kind of mess or residue on the flooring.

These fit Starmark brand treat holders.  I don't know if they would fit anything else.  There are various flavors.  There are times that I have to work on the weekends and I just want a treat to keep my dogs occupied...yet they lose interest in many of the  endurance  treats if they don't get something yummy...then pester me again, and I feel guilty and we repeat the cycle.These Starmark treats are great!  My dogs like all the flavors.  Basically, they can only get to a shallow knob on the top, so they hold it in their paws and lick/chew (well, try to chew, but can't get a grip)...for hours!The medium size is right for my pooches: a mini schnauzer and puggle (pug and beagle mix).  I would guess a lab would need a large.  The goal is for them NOT to get it all the way into their mouths, so they have to work for it.
My dog loves these treats, we tried a new flavor and she loved it also. It only takes her about an hour to get these out of the little ball.

My dog loves these. These last a long time for my 15 lb. Havanese. I use it in the blue (two sided), and pink (one sided) silicone balls. I subscribe to this. I recommend it, I will buy again, and I hope this helps someone and their dog.
She went to town chewing on this as soon as I put it in the treat ball and gave it to her.  She loves these!
Great both my great Dane and american bulldog go crazy for these. They make the room smell like vanilla too

Sadly my bento ball was broken by my puppy so I've been giving him these treats on its own. Thankfully he has been chewing them and swallowing some of them as well but so far no issues on it but I wouldn't buy them again as that would mean buying another bento ball, which in my opinion is too soft!
they lick it until it is gone.  then they try to get it out of the plastic toy.  definetly cheaper online than in the store.  order extras.
My dog loved these and was pleased that they took her a few sessions to eat.  Will order these again.
These do not last long in my house. my dogs seem to love this flavor the most. I am always seeking out the best price.

Tuffy toys do last longer than other toys in our household. Since I have two Siberian Huskies though, no toy last too long. This toy surprisingly lasted longer than any other Tuffy I have ever bought. On the Tuffy website, this bone shaped Tuffy receives at perfect 10 rating. I see why! I bought 2 of these in different colors. Every other toy I purchased is long gone except for these two Tuffy toys. If you have dogs that like to tear up toys, give this one a try. It is totally worth it!

This review covers three products I used together to create a  formula  for carpet cleaning that works in my household.  I have a multi-animal household, lots of builder grade carpeting, many area rugs of all kinds of fiber and thickness, tile and hardwood floors.  Keeping carpets clean has been a challenge at best, esp. considering that until I used these three products in concert, I never had truly clean carpet and old stains leeched back out with days after extensive shampooing.I bought the Bissell Big Green Complete Canister Vacuum 7700.  I added one capful of  Bissell 2X Pet Stain and Odor Portable Machine Formula  and one capful of  Fresh `N Clean Oxy Odor and Stain Remover for Dogs (Lambert Kay).   I used the caps that came with the respective cleansers.  It has been about a month since I did a thorough carpet shampooing and I have yet to see any previous stains reappear.  I used the solution on my tile floor in the bathroom and the grout came clean!  I have not used this method on my hardwood floors.I have tried using a mixture of the two cleansers in a spray bottle, as well as using the cleansers individually for spot cleaning.  Stains never fully come out unless I deep clean using the three products in concert.

For those of you not familiar with the symptoms, these were are some of the signs (our specific indications are in parentheses):**General confusion or disorientation**Wandering and/or pacing**Restlessness, sleeplessness at night**Acting  dazed  or staring off into space**Getting  stuck  in corners or small spaces (mostly under our kitchen table, boxed-in by the chair legs)**Seeming to be lost in familiar places (standing at the back gate in freezing rain after potty breaks, probably thinking it was the back door was our first clue)**Going to the wrong side of familiar doors (he would end up stuck behind partially opened doors with his nose facing the hinges)**Not responding well to his name or to commands he once knew (particularly noticeable during dinnertime, when he couldn't remember the words,  Time to eat dinner, Scooter )**Acting withdrawn; interacting less with familiar people and other pets (e.g., hiding out in the bedroom all day, even when we came home and yelled,  Let's go for a walk, Scooter! )**Forgetting house training; having  accidents  in areas where he never did before**Less enthusiastic about games, toys or foods that used to create excitementScooter was also shaking, panting, and unresponsive at certain times, which we (and the vet) took to be a seizure symptom... even though he had no history of epilepsy in any form. I did not want to put him on barbiturates since he is already on other medications for his arthritis, so after a good bit of research (and a quick call to the vet for an official  OK ) I started him on the Cholodin tabs.What a difference. After two full months of consistent dosing (3/4 tablet once a day), my 13-pound varmint hunter is tearing up the back yard, howling at the mailman, barking rabidly at falling leaves and wayward squirrels, shoving toys in our direction, and even shoving our other chihuahua mix out of the way for his favorite napping spot. I will not say he is completely symptom free, but he is no longer bumping into walls in broad daylight (his eyesight was fine at the last vet visit three months ago), getting stuck under the table, falling down stairs, staring into space during feeding time, and (most heartbreaking) not responding to the invitation to play with his favorite stuffed squirrel. We treated his arthritis withCosequin Joint Health Supplementand Deramaxx (NSAID, need a vet's prescription) and changed his food toUltra Dog Senior Dog Food Cans, 12-1/2-Ounce, 12 pack cansandPurina Veterinary Diets JM Joint Mobility Canine Formula Dry Dog Food 18 lb bagdry food, but his mental issues really started to turn around after we introduced the Cholodin.I HIGHLY recommend this supplement to anyone with a pet experiencing canine cognitive dysfunction.

I struggled in the beginning to get my Eclectus to eat this. I bought this food at the advice of my veterinarian. My eclectus also gets fresh organic fruits, veggies, bean mix and small amount of  nuts everyday. Fruits, bean mix and veggies are the main staple of his diet. He also had a tendency to want to eat sunflower seeds and other seeds only, which is not good for Eclectus to over eat. seeds. Especially not sunflower seeds. So, when taking him to the vet, my vet found that he was a bit low in weight and had a little bit of high liver enzymes. He asked if I was giving him pellets. I was giving him the natural Zupreem pellets but he didn't want to eat them. So what i did to get him to eat these is:First Week:.  I cut up the pellets and mashed it up with the juice from the blackberries I mixed in his favorite fruit. His favorite fruits are blueberries, pomegranate and blackberries. So I would squish the blackberry juice for example, all over the pellets to let them soak up the juice and mash it all up. Also left a few pellets in their usual size but let them soak up juice. Then I threw in the rest of the blackberry in with it. At first he would just eat the parts of the blackberries he could pick out. (I still continued to let him have seeds)Second Week: I cut pellets in half ( because he won't bite into nuts or pellets that are too hard) But I no longer mashed the pellets up.  He was picky so I continued the same thing ( Also I fed a few to my dogs and when he saw them eating it and heard the crunch crunch, he tried to pick up his pellets and then threw them down) (I ate a few myself, I have to say they are tasty and taste like sunflower seeds with no salt)Third Week: I began just soaking the pellets in his blackberry juice. (Juice of the blackberry only) ....continued his sunflower and seeds, but less of them (I had to go slow taking away his sunflower seeds because he actually got moody when I didn't give them to him)Fourth Week: Continue the same as third week but put less juice of the blackberry. (Really went down on seeds, like just a few)Fifth Week: By this time I cut only some of the Harrison's pellets up and left some the normal size. Tom Roudybush spent 16 years of nutritional research in the Department of Avian Sciences at the University of California, Tom studied a variety of birds, including 10 years of research on the nutritional requirements of companion birds. Even with only one accessory attached the flow is barely what I would call a bubble curtain. Its still a decent pump though, and the current airflow is more to my fishes liking.As far as noise level goes, this pump does make a hum, similar to the old computers of the floppy disk era. It's noticeable without some moderate white noise, but its no where near the drone of the 747 landing strip sounds the old pumps used to make. Unless you are listening for it, you likely won't even notice its there.The pump has rubber feet which keep it from wobbling around and may also help to deaden the sound a bit. There is only one air output on this one, but the box does include one T splitter. The pump also does not have an off switch, so if you are using for a purpose other than an aquarium, take that into account.  If you are planning on using lots of accessories (which require multiple airlines) you probably should invest in a pump with more than one output (again, this only has one). Or, if loss of airflow isn't an issue you can get a gang valve or some more splitters to connect your extra lines. Make sure to get a decent gang valve or check valves in case of power outage to protect your pump from back flow. Remember, every split off the main line will lessen your airflow with each addition.For now, this pump will suit my purposes. It seems built fairly well as pumps go. We've had to limit which rooms we play with the Orka because when I tossed the Jack it bounced at an odd angle, our boy chasing after it, almost sliding head first into a dangerous situation.  No bother, we just play in other rooms now!We supervise our boy when he has access to toys such as this.  So far this is amongst his favorites so he (usually) doesn't destroy his most prized possessions (our socks on the other hand...) I found the Orka Jack at our local veterinarian's office (well the store next door owned by the same veterinary team); I would CERTAINLY buy the Orka Jack and other Orka toys again!From the package:* Durable material great for power chewers* Hollow ends can be filled with treats if desired* Appealing  chewy  feel that dogs love! (ours do!) (and will gnaw on at great length)* It FLOATS and BOUNCES (yes yes yes Aiko loves playing with the Orka Jack his  kiddie pool !)* Multiple textures add interest and massage gums when chewed* Fun, unpredictable bounce pattern makes play more exciting (we found this to be true!)The ONLY Con... Made in China.
This was supposed to be long lasting but my dogs made quick work of it.  Recommended by my vet, though I'll stick with kong products (I've had much more success with these).

Got this as a replacement to one we've had a couple of years at least. Our dog is a real chewer and he likes this whether it has treats in it or not. He's pretty funny because if he gets tired of trying to get the treats out, he brings it over to us to get it out for him. So far it's as durable as the last one.

Well its much bigger than I anticipated, but that's okay. Its very sturdy and bounces in crazy patterns as I thought it would, but none of my dogs have so much as picked it up. I tried putting treats in it and that kept their attention briefly, but that was about it. I put a tug rope through it to try to peak their interest, but alas, no one care. My kids like it though haha

I own one pit bull and foster pit bulls, one at a time, for a local rescue group until they find their adoptive home.  These dogs have all been strong chewers.  I purchased this toy 6 months ago and it is one of my all-time favorite toys for the dogs (and one of the dogs favorites, too).  They love to chase it when I throw it, and they like to chew on it, too, for long periods of time.  Amazingly, it has survived very well, with only one bump having been chewed off to date.  What's more, it seems to be a toy that the dogs seek out.  I will buy this toy again.
This toy is really fun because it bounces all around so he plays with it and then tries to get the treats out.

Best toy ever, I don't think it will ever break.  I bought the large Orka for my 7 month old black lab and she loves it.  It bounces off in every direction, so she's zig zagging to catch it.  She also likes shaking this toy so watch out for your shins.

I loved the ORKA tennis balls for my power chewing pittie, so I thought I would try this. It is worth it's weight in gold if you have a chewer like mine! Now my lab has decided that he likes it too, so another one is on it's way! The Petstages ORKA toys have been lifesaver's for me and the bright blue color is an added bonus. We have plenty of grass and they stand out like beacons!
Our little silky terrier loves to fetch thisIt flies and so does she.....I love to buy all the pet stages toys and this was shipped very quickly
First time buying and both dogs love to play with this.  So far it has stood the test of many tug of wars.
Simply put. Dogs like it like we like potato chips. Have to order enough to last a week. Arrived within a week.
My Akita loves these.  She's very picky on treats but she will eat these every time without exception.  Good deal!!
The perfect toy/treat for our dog!!  When he wants a treat, we tell him to go get his  ball , he brings it to us, puts it in our hand, gets a treat and keeps him busy and happy for awhile!!
My dogs like gnawing on this.  It is a real pain, though to load the big treat discs into it.

My dogs love these balls, but after a few weeks, the ridge that holds in the treat started to fissure from them chewing on them, and now my dogs can get the treat out within a few minutes.  I prefer the medium ball (even for a small dog - my 6 lb maltese carries it all over the house with ease), the treats are impossible for them to get out, but keeps them very entertained.

My dogs love toys with treats inside. Its good stimulation for them to have to work at it. After they eat the included treat you can refill with more of the same or do what I do and improvise. I stuff Meaty Bones in it and it takes them a while to get it all out. It is a good toy for filling with treats and can be quite challenging for the dogs to get them out.

My 6 month old rottie pup bit out a fairly large hunk of the ball and swallowed it within the first 10 minutes of having this. Unacceptable. She still isn't at full strength on her  big girl  teeth and jaws. For the price, the size  Large , general description the name  Everlasting , I expected more than one 10 minute chewing session before the destruction and a dangerous intake of a piece of the actual ball into my puppy's body.

indistructable to datewill bounce like a ball - but also off centrecan put a few treats in it to leave with the doga favorite of mine and the dogs - but they do love the fireplug moreFANTASTIC PRODUCT FOR LABS

I waited until my dog was older to get this for his.  I was so excited because I thought it would last.  He is only a medium chewer and  it did not take him long to eat the treat, maybe an hr and a half.  That would have been fine.  The thing that i did not like was that the plastic can be easily eaten off.  My dog ripped apart the blue part and then later vomited the treats and plastic.  This is fine if your dog is a very light chewer but any stronger and I would be very careful.  I don't think it is worth the money.  I will stick with the himalayan bones
Our dogs love theses. We had to upgrade our smaller dog to the blue treat ball because it tougher than the small orange treat holder.
Have an agressive Yorkie and he had the biscuit removed in less than 10 minutes.  States it doesn't tear, but it rips. Wasted money.

Our dog just loves this thing. Goes nutz for it. The treat is really easy to get in and out if you use a screwdriver. Otherwise I've done some damage to my manicure! He will chew on this thing for two hours if we let him. Although he goes through them quicker than I'd like, especially if he has one for a while all at once, the treat gets more maleable from his slobber and he scraps it away easier. To avoid this, I only let him have it for 30 mins at a time usually, that way the treat lasts quite a bit longer.
Order extra refills as you can put two lockers in this ball. Dog loves it and cannot decide which side to lick first.

This toy came highly recommended to me by someone who also fosters pitbulls. This toy itself and this brand are about the only toys that a pitbull cannot destroy. The treat part is kinda yucky and only last about 2 minutes with an aggressive chewer that is able to pop it out and eat it right away. All-in-all still a great product for aggressive chewers. I just stick a large milk bone inside and that gives him something to work on. They also love to carry this around in their mouths and it bounces when they drop it.
GREAT idea!!!!  My dog loves it but be careful.  If your dog is smart he/she will find the way to remove it from its container.

I have a Boston Terrier puppy.  He is unable to remove the treats from this ball but still works at it.  Once I removed the treat he continued to use the ball as chew toy, and even includes it in his  fetch/retrieving game we play. The ball shows little wear and yet it is chewable .  A safe toy with resiliency.

I foster pups as well as own my own 25# dog.  This toy keeps the dogs busy for hours!!  Whent he insert treat runs out (which does last a long time) I can insert other treats or peanut butter to keep the fun going.  Easy to clean.  Very sturdy!

I had originally bought the Everlasting Medium Bento Ball for my lab mix (puppy at the time) and she absolutely LOVED it, so when I saw this one I just had to buy it for her.  I've had this toy for about a year and a half now and she doesn't even touch it. I'm not sure what the big difference is to her but she just doesn't like this one.  Hopefully everyone else's dog loves it though!

I've been searching for good dog toys that last longer than five seconds for my 10 month old, 60 lbs puppy. This is a keeper - it is still intact after several months, while most toys don't last the week or even the day. It's got great little pockets to hide high value treats in and can also withstand some chewing. I'm not sure how it fares against super power chewers but my average chewer it does very well.

This is the 2nd football we have had for my dog. The 1st one lasted a good three years before it was unusable. She loves getting her Milk Bones in the ball and whenever she wants a treat she goes and finds the ball and brings it to us. This has worked great for us, I saw some reviews where the dog chewed through it right away.. must have something to do with the power in the jaws or something. My dog is a 50 lb. mixed breed, Border Collie, Black Lab., Blue Heeler, Pit Bull.. so maybe she got the Lab's soft mouth.
This keeps my dogs attention when we are outside. They cannot determine which way it will bounce and keeps them on their toes

My dog is very rough on toys.  These footballs last longer than some of the other junk I've bought for her.  She always pulls all the fuzz off it on the first day, but she loves chewing on the rubber underneath. This toy maintains its squeak for a long time.
